**About the role:**
BSI is embarking on a major global Finance Transformation, including the implementation of SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) Planning as part of our wider SAP S/4HANA programme.
We are looking for a SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) Business Analyst to help bridge the gap between our Finance teams and the technology and implementation teams delivering the programme.
SAC will become a key platform for BSI's FP&A and Commercial Finance teams, supporting budgeting, forecasting and long-range planning. This role will help ensure the solution not only works technically, but is ready for Finance teams to use successfully as it is deployed across BSI.
You will work closely with FP&A, Commercial Finance, regional Finance teams, Deloitte and the wider transformation programme to understand business requirements, support solution design, coordinate testing and data validation, prepare users for deployment and support adoption following go-live.
This is very much a Finance Transformation role rather than a BAU Finance position. You will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience of a major global SAC implementation, working across multiple deployment waves and supporting Finance teams through significant process and system change.
**Responsibilities:**
* Develop a strong understanding of BSI's new SAP Analytics Cloud Planning solution and how it will support FP&A and Commercial Finance.
* Work with Finance stakeholders to gather, challenge, document and validate business and functional requirements.
* Help translate Finance requirements into clear functional specifications for Deloitte and technology delivery teams.
* Support the design of future-state SAC processes covering budgeting, forecasting, rolling forecasts and long-range planning.
* Support the design and validation of SAC planning models, dimensions, hierarchies, workflows, approval structures, planning calendars and security requirements.
* Help define the readiness and success criteria that must be achieved before SAC is deployed into each country or region.
* Support deployment activities across multiple global rollout waves, ensuring Finance teams, processes, data and systems are ready for go-live.
* Plan and coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT), including developing test scenarios, scripts and acceptance criteria.
* Work directly with Finance users to ensure the system has been thoroughly tested ahead of deployment. System readiness, user testing and training for each deployment were identified as core priorities for the role during the briefing.
* Support data mapping, migration, validation and reconciliation between existing and future Finance systems.
* Log, track and support the resolution of defects alongside Deloitte and wider programme teams.
* Develop training materials, user documentation and work instructions and support end-user training and onboarding.
* Support change management and business readiness activities, building relationships with Finance super-users and champions across BSI.
* Provide post-go-live hyper-care and help ensure new SAC processes become successfully embedded within the Finance community.
* Support the ongoing administration and continuous improvement of SAC following implementation.

* At least 5 years' experience within FP&A, Commercial Finance, Finance Transformation, Finance Systems or Business Analysis.
* Previous experience working directly with FP&A or Finance Business Partnering teams, with a strong understanding of their processes and requirements. This was identified as particularly important during the hiring-manager briefing.
* Good knowledge of budgeting, forecasting, planning and management reporting processes.
* Experience documenting business processes and translating Finance requirements into functional requirements or specifications.
* Experience supporting a Finance system implementation, transformation or migration programme.
* Hands-on SAP Analytics Cloud experience would be highly advantageous; experience with SAP S/4HANA, SAC or a comparable enterprise planning platform will also be considered.
* Experience moving from one budgeting or planning system to another would be particularly valuable, as it provides first-hand understanding of the user and change journey involved.
* Experience planning and executing UAT, including developing testing scenarios and working with end users.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities and the ability to manage multiple workstreams within a complex transformation programme.

# Introduction to Role & Team
At Bumble, our mission is to create a world where healthy and equitable relationships and friendships thrive, and our Legal team plays an important role in protecting the ideas, brands, technology, and experiences that bring that mission to life. As Lead Legal Counsel within our IP team, you’ll be a senior subject-matter expert helping Bumble navigate complex intellectual property questions across our brands, products, technology, content, and creative work. You’ll independently lead significant IP matters and shape practical strategies in close partnership with colleagues across Legal, Marketing, Creative, Brand, Design, Product, and Engineering, combining Courage and Curiosity with strong commercial judgement. You’ll also help us explore the opportunities and risks created by AI and other emerging technologies, using AI thoughtfully in your own work while applying human judgement, care, and accountability to the outcomes.
# What You’ll Do
* Shape and execute Bumble’s global intellectual property strategy in partnership with Legal leadership, translating business, brand, product, and technology priorities into practical approaches to protection, portfolio management, licensing, and enforcement.
* Take ownership of significant matters across Bumble’s international trademark, copyright, patent, domain name, trade secret, and broader digital asset portfolio, working with external counsel and specialist providers to protect strategically important intellectual property.
* Collaborate with purpose across Marketing, Creative, Brand, Design, Product, and Engineering, providing practical rights-clearance and IP advice from early concept and development through launch, including trademarks, copyright, publicity rights, creator and talent rights, user-generated content, and third-party materials.
* Independently lead complex IP enforcement and dispute matters, including infringement, oppositions, litigation support, and evidence management, applying commercial judgement to determine where action can deliver meaningful protection for Bumble’s brands and innovation.
* Advise on the creation, ownership, protection, licensing, and commercialisation of Bumble-developed intellectual property, and draft and negotiate sophisticated IP arrangements including licences, coexistence agreements, assignments, merchandising arrangements, technology agreements, and strategic partnerships.
* Partner with Product and Engineering on patent strategy, software development, open-source software, and innovation protection, while advising on emerging IP questions involving generative AI, training data, provenance, ownership, licensing, and infringement risk.

## Job Description
**Job Title: Data & Reporting Administrator**
**Reports to: Head of Talent Acquisition**
**Type: Permanent, full time 35 hours per week**
**Location: Hybrid, 1/2 days a week in our Burntwood head office**
**Salary: Up to £32,000 per annum DOE**
**About the role**
As our Data & Reporting Administrator, you’ll play a key role in supporting the Talent Acquisition team through accurate data, insightful reporting and effective recruitment systems.
You’ll take ownership of recruitment data and system administration, producing regular and ad-hoc reports that help the team understand performance, identify trends and make informed decisions. You’ll also help ensure our recruitment systems are well maintained, data is high quality, and processes run smoothly throughout the candidate journey.
Working closely with Talent Acquisition, People team, hiring managers and other stakeholders, you’ll be a trusted point of contact for recruitment data and systems, helping to improve reporting, streamline processes and make better use of our recruitment technology.
You’ll act as the SME for our ATS (ICIMS), championing the system as the single source of truth for TA reporting and data.
**About Busy Bees**
Founded in 1983, Busy Bees is the UK’s largest early years provider and the third largest globally, there has never been a more exciting time to join our growing team.
**About the Benefits**
* Sector leading Family Leave.
* Big Benefits. Dedicated 24/7 employee benefits platform Hive (Reward Gateway)
* with retail, cinema, and travel discounts
* 35% Childcare discount.
* 33 days holiday inclusive of bank holidays and an extra day off for your birthday every year
* Further Training and development.
**What You’ll Be Doing**
**Recruitment Systems Administration**
* Act as a key administrator for our Applicant Tracking System (ATS) and other Talent Acquisition systems.
* Maintain system data, user access, workflows, recruitment templates, fields and configuration.
* Create and maintain user accounts, permissions and access levels.
* Support the onboarding and offboarding of system users.
* Troubleshoot system issues and liaise with system providers or IT where required.
* Maintain recruitment processes and workflows within the ATS, ensuring they remain accurate and fit for purpose.
* Support system testing, upgrades and implementation of new functionality.
* Develop and maintain system guidance and user documentation.
* Provide first-line support and advice to recruiters and hiring managers on system queries.
**Data & Reporting**
* Produce accurate and timely recruitment reports and dashboards for Talent Acquisition and senior stakeholders.
* Maintain regular reporting on recruitment activity, including vacancies, applications, interviews, offers, hires, time-to-hire and recruitment pipeline data.
* Prepare ad-hoc analysis and reports in response to business requirements.
* Maintain reporting schedules and ensure recurring reports are delivered within agreed deadlines.
* Support the development and improvement of recruitment dashboards and management information.
* Ensure recruitment data is consistently defined, recorded and reported across the team.
**Data Quality & Governance**
* Carry out regular data-quality checks within recruitment systems.
* Investigate and correct inaccurate, incomplete or duplicate records.
* Support compliance with data protection, retention and information governance requirements.
* Ensure recruitment records are maintained appropriately throughout the candidate lifecycle.
* Assist with audits of recruitment data and system access.
* Maintain accurate records of system changes and reporting definitions.
**Talent Acquisition Support**
* Support recruitment campaigns and bulk recruitment activity through accurate system configuration and reporting.
* Work with recruiters and hiring managers to ensure recruitment activity is correctly recorded in the ATS.
* Provide data and insight to support workforce and recruitment planning.
**Key skills and experience**
* Experience in data, reporting, HR, recruitment operations or Talent Acquisition.
* Proven system administration experience, ideally within an ATS, HRIS or similar system.
* Experience managing users, access permissions, workflows, configuration and system data.
* Experience producing regular and ad-hoc recruitment/HR reports and MI.
* Strong Excel skills, including data analysis, manipulation and presentation.
* Experience identifying and resolving data-quality issues.
* Strong attention to detail, organisation and ability to meet deadlines.
* Confident communicating system and data issues to non-technical stakeholders.
**Desirable Experience**
* Experience administering Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle, iCIMS, Greenhouse, SmartRecruiters, Workable or similar ATS/HRIS.
* Experience developing Power BI or other recruitment dashboards.
* Experience supporting system implementations, upgrades and configuration changes.
* Understanding of recruitment processes and the candidate lifecycle.
* Knowledge of GDPR and recruitment data protection.
* Experience working with large datasets and producing management information.
If you’re passionate about recruitment data, systems and continuous improvement, and enjoy turning data into meaningful insight, **we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and join our Talent Acquisition team.**

## Fresh Food, Happy Dogs.
We believe dogs deserve the healthiest, most natural and tastiest meals - with none of the nasties. That's why we make FRESHly prepared food, cooked just like you would at home and delivered direct to our customers in perfect portions. As a B-Corp certified company, you're joining a sustainable business that genuinely cares about our people, our products and our impact on the planet. Our goal is simple: to help dogs live healthier, happier, and longer lives, while leaving humans smiling after every interaction.
We've come a long way since our co-founders (Kev & Dave), hand delivered the very first Butternut Box. Today, we feed hundreds of thousands of hungry dogs across the UK and Europe - but we won't stop until we're feeding dogs everywhere. To get there, we need a team of brilliant people who share that ambition to come and work for us.
## | The job:
We are searching for an outgoing, hardworking, all-around great communicator who cares passionately about the experience that our customers receive.
You will be joining an exceptional team to be the eyes and ears of Butternut Box, talking to our customers on a daily basis to resolve all customer queries. All incoming live customer contact will go through you, especially making use of email, phone, live chat, and social media channels. You will be empowered to help shape our customer journey and come up with new ways to make people's lives easier and happier.
We want you to tell us in your initial application what your favourite dog breed is and why. The right fit will be someone who is motivated by the idea of bringing moments of happiness to the people (and dogs!) we serve and is excited by the idea of working in an exciting business from within our office in White City, London.
This role is for 39 hours per week, Monday - Friday 9am to 6pm. This is a hybrid role with office days on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday.
**Some of your day-to-day activities will include:**
* Being the face and voice of Butternut Box to new and existing customers.
* Using communication tools including phone, email, live chat and social media to keep customers informed.
* Dealing with a wide range of queries, issues and feedback from our current and potential customer base.
* Bringing happy moments to the people (and dogs!) we serve.
* Passing on customer insights & feedback for us to turn those into strategic decisions for the future of the business.
* Helping to form our culture and voice, and bring a fresh pair of eyes to everything.
We need to be accessible to our customers at all times, this means that for the majority of this role you will need be confident and have a passion for helping them on the phone.
## | What we're looking for:
* A passion for problem solving and finding resolutions independently.
* You have experience in a customer service role.
* Experience using a Macbook also a bonus but not essential.
* Ready to get stuck in and work hard.
* Good numerical reasoning skills and the ability to understand complex plans and discounts.
* Exceptional communication skills, both spoken and written.
* Kind, giving and thoughtful.
* You can work autonomously to a very high standard, and also thrive as part of a team.
* Eager to learn and improve.
* Genuine, honest, reliable and adaptable.
* You love dogs.
## | The interview process:
1. Initial call with your dedicated Talent Acquisition Partner, carried out remotely.
2. Sometimes the process will include a take home task, or a presentation of some kind.
3. Skills interview, usually carried out remotely.
4. Behaviours interview, usually carried out in person.
5. Depending on the seniority of the role you're applying for, there may be a final Leadership interview as a final step.
*We usually expect our interview process to take 3-5 weeks, end to end.*
## | Our benefits:
* 25 days holiday (plus 8 bank holidays) and an additional day for every year of service up to 5 years
* 5 additional, paid 'paws' days off per year dedicated to your learning, development or personal wellbeing. Hit pause when you need it most
* £500 personal learning & development budget to sharpen your skills
* Share options grant - everyone owns a piece of Butternut's success.
* A significant discount on our Fresh food, to keep your own dogs as healthy as our customers
* Enhanced parental leave
* Flexible core working hours
* Cycle to work scheme
* Pension with NEST
* Private Medical Insurance with Vitality
* Private Dental Insurance with Bupa
* Paid time off for fertility treatments and pregnancy loss
* Paid sabbaticals for squad members with 5 or more years service at Butternut
* Discounted gym access through MyGymDiscounts
* Lots of office dogs (Ajax, Peggy, Chief, Louis, Hansen, Winnie and many more...)
## | Important things to note:
* There are 4 stages to this interview process. If successful after your application you will be invited for a call with our internal recruiter. The second stage is a written task where you'll be asked a mixture of questions, some based on your experience and some situational based. The third and fourth stage will be face to face interviews with members of the Customer Love leadership team.
* The set hours listed could change based on the unforeseen needs of the Customer Love team and Butternut Box, which is a seven day per week operation. If there are to be any changes to your hours or days of work, reasonable notice and consultation will be given.
* We recommend getting your application in as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the role early.
* Our team thrives on collaboration. We spend **3 days a week in our West London office** (Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday) and 2 days working from wherever you're most productive. Because being together is a big part of our culture, we're looking for someone within a comfortable commutable distance to London.
* We're a small (but mighty!) recruitment team. We aim to respond to everyone personally, but if we're flooded with brilliant applications, we may need to close the role early. We appreciate your patience while we review applications.
* For this specific role, we're unable to offer visa sponsorship, so you'll need the right to work in the UK.
## | We believe in a **seat at the table for everyone.**
Butternut Box is an equal opportunity employer. We believe that to make the best food for *all* dogs, we need a team that represents *all* humans. We celebrate different nationalities, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We are specifically committed to increasing representation from underrepresented groups. We want a strong, diverse team built from different identities and lived experiences. We're not perfect, but we are dedicated to the ongoing work of building an inclusive, supportive place where you can do the best work of your career.

# Executive Assistant & Office Manager (Climate Tech)
London, UK
## About CarbonChain
The fight against Climate Change is evolving rapidly. Climate tech is changing. The first wave was reporting. The next is treating carbon the way companies treat money: as a way to decide what to buy, who to sell to, and which incentives to claim. Around the world, carbon is becoming a condition of trade. Border taxes, free allocations, green premiums, cheaper capital. It looks a lot like the post-war rebuild: governments put capital and tax incentives on the table, and the companies that could keep the books moved first. The missing piece then was bookkeeping. The missing piece now is the same, carbon accounting. CarbonChain is that bookkeeping. We turn messy, real-world supply-chain data into numbers a trader, a sustainability lead, or a CFO will actually use. We want people who are agents of change, who feel the impact of climate change and know there is no way around it to create a better future for every being. People who know the customer is the truth of how a company thrives. People who treat data as the fuel for how fast society can change. People who use AI to accelerate the cause for good by working through an AI lens first to automate repetitive tasks and analyse data. Finally, people who enjoy working with people. ### Our Product
We help the world's largest commodity producers and traders measure and cut emissions, with verified primary data where we can get it and defensible defaults where we cannot. The platform turns operational and supplier files into decision-grade carbon and compliance insight: sourcing, CBAM, product and corporate footprints, reporting customers and regulators will stand behind. We organise carbon accounting around the user in four contexts at once: * **Immediate:** the tools in front of them
* **Internal:** how they work with colleagues
* **External:** how they work with suppliers and customers
* **Societal:** how they work with society, governments, and disclosing bodies
The data we hold is only useful if it makes all four of those jobs easier. ## About the Role
We're hiring an Executive Assistant & Office Manager to run point on two things that shape how CarbonChain works day to day: keeping our leadership's time protected and well used, and making our Camden office somewhere the team wants to be. Reporting to the Head of Operations, you'll split your time between being a right hand to our C-level leadership and making our Camden office run well. This is a brand-new role at CarbonChain, and that's the interesting part: there's no handover, no inherited process, no "this is how it's always been done." You'll define what excellent executive and office support looks like here. When you define the role, expect to use AI daily to draft, schedule, triage, so the job asks more of your judgement and less of your time on admin. That's a deliberate trade we've built into how this role works to align with our wider company’s direction. ### What You'll Do
**Executive support** * Our leadership travels often and keeps a full diary. Own making that manageable: sharp calendar judgement, end-to-end travel coordination (itineraries, accommodation, contingency plans), and the instinct to protect their time without being asked.
* Support inbox management, correspondence, and follow-ups, and act as a reliable point of contact between leadership and internal or external partners.
* Handle expense reporting and reconciliation accurately and on time.
* Prepare and coordinate materials for leadership, board, or all-hands meetings: agendas, pre-reads, minutes, and follow-up on action items.
* Track action items, deadlines, and workflows across ongoing projects, so nothing falls through when priorities shift.
* Spot friction before it becomes a problem, and fix the process behind it, not just the one instance.
* Handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion, as standard.
**Workplace experience and culture** * Serve as the primary point of contact for our Camden office: employees and guests, with a warm and professional welcome.
* Make our Camden office a place people want to come into: weekly catering, a stocked snacks section, and the everyday moments that build a team.
* Run our offsites. Keep the leadership team's workshops and room bookings sorted so their time together isn't wasted on logistics.
* Support internal communications and culture initiatives, and look for opportunities to improve the day-to-day experience of the office.
**Office operations and administration** * Own the day-to-day running of the office: supplies, equipment, and the space itself, so it's always functional, tidy, and well stocked.
* Maintain basic office administration: mail, deliveries, and correspondence.
* Own new team member onboarding and offboarding end-to-end. A new starter's first week should feel looked after, and someone leaving should have the smoothest farewell.
* Build and maintain our SOPs in Notion, so how CarbonChain actually works lives somewhere real, not in one person's head.
### What We're Looking For
* 5+ years of experience in an EA, office management, workplace experience, or operations role.
* Strong judgement: you can tell what's urgent, what can wait, and what needs to be escalated, without needing to be told, and you're comfortable with ambiguity rather than waiting for step-by-step direction.
* You already use AI tools, e.g. Claude or scheduling agents, as part of how you work. You are comfortable using AI day to day to move faster on the transactional tasks, so you can spend your own time on what actually needs a human - judgement, prioritisation, and reading the room.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, comfortable with executives, colleagues, and external partners alike.
* Discretion and maturity with confidential information.
* A proactive mindset: you spot what's needed before it's asked for, and you deal with the cause rather than just the symptom.
* Care about culture and the small details that make an office a good place to work
**Nice to have** * Experience in a high-growth start-up, scale-up, or another fast-paced professional environment.
* Exposure to budgeting, vendor negotiation, or basic bookkeeping.
* Experience supporting a founder or C-level executive directly.
### How We Work
As a hybrid co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the UK and US. This role would be located 3d/week in our London LABS Camden office space. You will need the right to work in the UK. ## What We Offer
**Meaningful impact and accelerated growth** This is a rare opportunity to work on technology that directly addresses the climate crisis while shaping the future of a fast-growing company. You'll have significant influence over our company’s direction. You'll tackle diverse challenges, work across the full stack of problems and own meaningful projects from start to finish. If you want to learn quickly, take on real responsibility, and see the direct results of your work, this is the place to do it. **Competitive salary and benefits:** * 28 days annual leave
* £500 home office setup allowance
* £2,000 annual learning allowance
* Private healthcare
* Company pension incl. salary sacrifice options
* Generous parental leave policy
* Weekly team lunches in the office
* Office gym, and cycle to work scheme
* Remote work contribution of £1,000 towards expenses for 1-week abroad
CarbonChain values diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds. If you think your skills and experience match what we’re looking for and you’d like to join the next Climate Tech industry unicorn, please get in touch!
You can find out more about interviewing at CarbonChain at https://www.carbonchain.com/careers/interview-process.

# Head of AI Transformation
## At Chip, our mission is to make our customers wealthier. An app to build your long-term wealth across savings, investments and pensions.
We usually respond within three days
AI is going to fundamentally change how companies operate. At Chip, we don't want to bolt AI onto the way we work today – we want to use it to rethink how we operate, make decisions and scale.
We're looking for a Head of AI Transformation to work directly with our COO and leadership team to make that happen.
This role will sit at the heart of how Chip operates and evolves. Alongside driving our AI transformation, you'll work directly with the COO on our broader operating model – how the organisation is structured, how work flows across teams, how decisions get made, how priorities translate into execution, and how we create the operating leverage required to scale.
This is not an AI strategy role where success means producing a roadmap. And it isn't a traditional programme management role.
It's a business transformation and operating role, with AI as one of the most important tools available to you.
You'll identify where AI, automation and changes to the way we operate can materially improve the business, turn those opportunities into executable initiatives and drive them through to measurable results.
You'll work across every part of Chip – Operations, Customer Service, Finance, Risk & Compliance, Marketing, Product, Engineering, People and our leadership teams – looking horizontally across the organisation rather than optimising functions in isolation.
You'll help us understand how work actually flows through Chip, where time and capacity are being consumed, where processes are unnecessarily manual, where ownership or decision-making is unclear, where organisational friction is slowing us down, and where AI or changes to our operating model can enable us to operate faster, smarter and at greater scale.
Most importantly, you'll make things happen.
**What you can expect to be doing:**
* Work directly with the COO on how Chip operates and scales. Help evolve our operating model as the business grows – looking at organisational structures, accountabilities, decision-making, governance, ways of working and how teams interact across the company.
* Identify and solve cross-business operating problems. Some of the biggest opportunities won't belong to a single function. You'll get underneath issues that cut across teams, establish what's really causing them and drive the changes required to fix them.
* Improve how strategy turns into execution. Help create stronger connections between company priorities, functional plans and the work actually happening across the organisation – ensuring we can see where resources are being deployed, where delivery is off track and where leadership intervention is required.
* Drive operating leverage. Constantly look for opportunities to increase the amount Chip can deliver without proportionately increasing cost or headcount – through better processes, clearer accountability, technology, automation, AI and changes to how work is organised.
* Challenge organisational complexity. Identify unnecessary hand-offs, duplicated activity, unclear ownership, excessive reporting, slow decision-making and processes that have accumulated as the business has grown – and simplify them.
* Help the COO maintain a business-wide view of performance and execution. Surface emerging issues, dependencies, capacity constraints and opportunities that might otherwise remain within individual functions.
* Lead selected COO-sponsored strategic and operational initiatives. Where an important business problem or opportunity cuts across existing organisational boundaries, take ownership of getting it understood, structured and delivered.
* Own Chip's business-wide AI transformation programme, translating our ambitions for AI into a prioritised portfolio of initiatives with clear owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.
* Find the highest-value opportunities across the business. Get underneath how teams actually operate, identify friction, manual work, duplicated effort and broken workflows, and determine where AI, automation or operating-model change can create meaningful commercial or operational value.
* Turn opportunities into working solutions. Take ideas from discovery and business case through prototyping, implementation, adoption and measurement rather than stopping at recommendations.
* Build a clear transformation and AI value pipeline. Prioritise initiatives based on measurable business impact – including capacity released, cost avoided, revenue enabled, customer outcomes improved, risk reduced and speed increased.
* Redesign workflows, not just automate individual tasks. Look across functions and end-to-end processes to identify opportunities to fundamentally simplify how work gets done.
* Create visibility across the organisation. Help us use tools, data and AI to understand what teams are working on, where capacity is being deployed, what is blocking delivery and where intervention will have the greatest impact.
* Drive cross-functional execution. Bring together Product, Engineering, Operations, Data and business teams to deliver transformation initiatives that don't sit neatly within one function.
* Strengthen organisational accountability. Help ensure important cross-functional initiatives have clear ownership, decisions are made at the right level and commitments translate into delivery.
* Build AI into the way Chip works. Challenge teams to consider AI and automation as a default part of designing new processes rather than something added afterwards.
* Develop scalable operating systems and workflows. Work with platforms such as Linear and other business tools to create greater transparency, stronger prioritisation and increasingly intelligent workflows across Chip.
* Use AI to transform management information and reporting. Reduce manual reporting, improve the quality and timeliness of insight and make it easier for leaders to understand what is happening across the business and where action is required.
* Improve the operating rhythm of the business. Help ensure leadership meetings, business reviews, planning and reporting processes are driven by high-quality information, clear decisions and follow-through rather than simply producing more meetings and reporting.
* Create the measurement framework for transformation. Establish baselines and track whether initiatives are actually delivering the productivity, financial and operational benefits expected.
* Drive adoption. Technology alone doesn't create transformation. Work with teams and leaders to change behaviours, embed new ways of working and ensure new capabilities are actually used.
* Bring external thinking into Chip. Stay close to developments in AI, agentic workflows, automation and emerging operating models, and rapidly translate relevant developments into practical opportunities for Chip.
* Be a constructive agitator. Challenge existing processes, assumptions and priorities and push the organisation to move faster where the opportunity warrants it.
* Work directly with the COO, ExCo and senior leadership team, providing clear visibility of progress, surfacing blockers and opportunities, and being prepared to challenge senior stakeholders when delivery isn't moving quickly enough.
**What we’re looking for:**
We're deliberately looking for an unusual combination of skills.
You need to understand technology, but you don't need to be an AI engineer. You need to understand transformation, but we don't want someone whose primary skill is running a programme plan.
You also need to understand how businesses actually operate. You'll be equally interested in why a decision takes three weeks, why ownership between two teams isn't clear or why five teams are doing versions of the same thing as you are in what the latest AI model can do.
We're looking for someone who combines commercial instinct, AI fluency, strong operating judgement and relentless execution.
**You'll probably have:**
* Significant experience delivering technology, AI, automation, digital or business/operating-model transformation in a fast-moving organisation.
* Experience working on broader business transformation, organisational effectiveness, operating models or complex cross-functional change.
* A strong understanding of how high-performing organisations operate – including accountability, decision-making, prioritisation, governance, management information and operating cadence.
* A strong practical understanding of modern AI – including LLMs, agentic AI, workflow automation and the rapidly evolving AI tooling ecosystem.
* Evidence that you've implemented AI or automation into real business processes and can demonstrate the impact it delivered.
* The ability to understand a business process quickly, break it down and identify where technology, AI, data, process redesign or organisational change can materially improve it.
* The ability to move comfortably between strategic and operational problems – from thinking about how part of the organisation should operate to getting underneath the detail of a broken workflow.
* Strong commercial judgement. You naturally think about value, ROI, opportunity cost and where limited organisational capacity should be deployed.
* Exceptional programme and execution skills. You create clarity from ambiguity, establish ownership, maintain momentum and don't allow important initiatives to disappear into organisational gaps.
* Strong analytical skills and comfort using data to establish baselines, quantify opportunities and measure results.
* The ability to operate horizontally across an organisation and influence people who don't report to you.
* The confidence and credibility to work directly with executives and senior leaders, including constructively challenging them when necessary.
* The judgement to know when a problem needs technology, when it needs process change, when it needs clearer accountability – and when it simply needs someone to make a decision.
* A bias towards experimentation and delivery. You're comfortable prototyping something quickly, learning from it and improving it rather than waiting for perfect information.
* Excellent communication skills. You can turn complex technology and operational problems into clear decisions and actions.
* A genuine obsession with how AI is changing the way companies operate and how the best companies are redesigning themselves around it.
**Nice to have**
* Experience in fintech, financial services or another regulated environment.
* Experience working in a high-growth technology business.
* Experience working directly with a COO, CEO or executive leadership team on business-wide priorities.
* Experience with operating-model design or organisational transformation.
* Experience implementing agentic AI or AI-enabled workflows at organisational scale.
* Hands-on experience with tools across the emerging AI and automation ecosystem.
* Experience with workflow and work-management platforms such as Linear and using the data within them to improve organisational performance.
* Experience building business cases and measuring realised benefits from transformation programmes.
* Enough technical depth to prototype, interrogate solutions and work effectively with engineers and data teams without needing them to translate everything for you.
**What success looks like**
This role won't be measured by the number of AI tools Chip deploys.
And it won't only be measured by our AI programme.
It will be measured by whether Chip becomes a better, simpler and more scalable organisation as a result of your work.
Within your first year, we would expect to see a visible portfolio of AI-enabled and broader business transformation underway across Chip, with clear evidence of processes being simplified or eliminated, manual activity reducing, decision-making becoming faster and better informed, and teams able to handle greater scale without equivalent growth in headcount.
We would expect greater clarity around priorities and accountability, fewer organisational hand-offs, better visibility of execution across teams, faster resolution of cross-functional problems and a stronger connection between what the company has decided is important and where its resources are actually being deployed.
We should have significantly better visibility of how work flows through the organisation, where our capacity is being deployed and where opportunities exist to improve performance.
Our leadership team should have better information with which to run the business, clearer visibility of where intervention is required and greater confidence that decisions and commitments are translating into action.
Most importantly, AI should increasingly become part of how Chip operates, rather than something the business occasionally uses, and our operating model should continue to evolve to take advantage of what AI makes possible.
**What we’re really looking for:** ✍️
We want someone who looks at the way a business operates and instinctively thinks: there has to be a better way of doing this.
Then goes and builds it.
Sometimes the answer will be AI. Sometimes it will be automation. Sometimes it will be changing a process, removing a meeting, redesigning a workflow, clarifying who owns something or challenging why we're doing something at all.
That's an important distinction in this role. We don't want someone looking for problems to solve with AI. We want someone looking for the biggest opportunities to make Chip better – who happens to understand deeply how AI changes the range of solutions available to us.
You'll be naturally curious about AI and probably already use it constantly. You'll experiment with new tools because you want to understand what they can do, not because someone has asked you to.
But being excited about AI isn't enough.
You'll need the commercial instincts to identify which opportunities actually matter, the judgement to prioritise them, and the persistence to get them implemented across a busy organisation.
You'll also need to be fascinated by how organisations work: how decisions happen, why execution gets stuck, where accountability becomes blurred, how information flows and how great businesses maintain pace as they become larger and more complex.
You'll be comfortable moving between very different conversations – interrogating a workflow with an operational team in the morning, working through an AI solution with engineers in the afternoon, unblocking a cross-functional business problem, and presenting the business case and delivery status to senior leadership later that day.
You'll have strong opinions, loosely held. You'll challenge us. You'll expect pace. And when something gets stuck between teams, you'll be the person who gets it moving again.
You'll effectively become one of the COO's key levers for making the organisation work better – able to move across functions, spot problems and opportunities that aren't visible from within individual teams, and turn them into action.
If you're looking for a role where you can help redesign how an entire company operates as AI transforms the workplace, this could be a particularly interesting time to join Chip.

CloudBees helps organizations build, run, and govern software factories, giving enterprises the confidence to ship software better, faster, and safer.

Company Profile CloudMargin is an award winning, growth-stage FinTech company offering an innovative Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) service. CloudMargin's Platform team owns the cloud infrastructure our product runs on, and serves everyone across the business who depends on it, from the engineers building on it to the client-facing and operational teams whose work runs through it. The primary purpose of this role is to own that team's backlog, where three kinds of demand compete for the same capacity: enabling other teams to move quickly, keeping the estate secure, current and observable, and controlling what it costs to run. Almost none of this work is visible to clients, and all of it is felt by them. The role is accountable for making those trade-offs deliberately and defensibly, rather than letting the loudest request win. This entails:
Understanding Demand: Gathering needs from wherever they arise. Shaping the Roadmap: Working with the Lead Site Reliability Engineer to sequence strategic initiatives, from rapid client environment provisioning to migrations onto managed services, against the maintenance and remediation the estate needs.
Making Platform Value Legible: Articulating what infrastructure investment buys, whether onboarding speed, engineering throughput, security posture or run cost, so that platform work is understood, funded and adopted.

# Software Engineer
Full-time | On-site | London, UK
CodeSpeak is an Agentic Engineering Toolkit: a set of tools to make AI coding work well for production-grade software projects.
Coding agents are amazing for prototypes, one-offs, and hobby projects. Yet, for serious production, results are more mixed:
* the amount of slop in codebases is growing, and they become less and less maintainable (GitClear-26),
* people can’t keep up with reviews,
* and more and more areas in projects accumulate “comprehension debt” (nobody really understands how they work).
As a result, engineering leaders are seeing more incidents per PR (+23.5%, see Cortex-26). In other words, **people ship slop, and it’s starting to bite them**. “The Claude Code moment” happened in late 2025, so what we see today is not even the full extent of the consequences.
At CodeSpeak, we believe three simple things:
* AI coding tools can help people make quality production software;
* Nobody wants to ship slop, people just don’t have the right tools to remain on top of their codebases;
* While coding may be solved by models, Software Engineering is still a human job.
**CodeSpeak’s Vision**. The prompts we give to coding agents are a new proto-language that is emerging right now. And we want to make it into a good, usable production language. The valuable part is that these prompts contain the *intent* behind the code. The resulting code can be generated from it, therefore it must be a complete description of the system. Right now, this description is very messy, and we want to make it clean and useful.
The proto-language of prompts that’s emerging right now is at the “spaghetti prompts” stage:
* important decisions are largely buried in session logs that nobody reads (because they are often not very readable),
* exploration, ideation, and prototyping are mixed with careful construction of lasting architectures,
* there’s no modularity, abstraction, or static checks on prompts.
To fix this, we need to do the same things we did to fix spaghetti code: we need to organise the high-level intent from prompts into always-up-to-date, reusable logical modules that humans and agents can navigate. Like modules in a programming language, but on the next level. That’s Software Engineering for the age of AI, and CodeSpeak is building tools that make it possible.
**CodeSpeak’s Current Approach**. We believe that user intent is the real primary artifact, and code is just what's derived from it. Right now, we're building an engine that captures this intent from session transcripts, distills it into structured requirements, grounds them in the code, and enforces them as the codebase changes.
These requirements become the layer developers actually work through, across the entire development process. For example:
* When an agent starts a new feature, CodeSpeak injects the relevant requirements into its context, so it builds with the rest of the system in mind.
* When a new prompt in a chat contradicts older requirements, a code isn’t written until the conflict is resolved.
* Code review starts from the requirement-level diff: what intent changed, what constraints were added or removed, and whether the implementation still satisfies them.
See more in our blog, and this is only the beginning. Let’s talk about what will come next when we meet.

CodeSpeak is founded by Andrey Breslav, creator of Kotlin – a language used by millions of developers every day. Around him is a team that has built the tools other engineers rely on, at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph, and Elastic. # Retail Engineer (Solution Delivery), UK
London, United Kingdom
Full-time
CommerceClarity is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on what you can do and how you work with people.
## What the role is about
Retailers still run too much catalog work through spreadsheets and copy-paste: filling missing attributes, adapting products to each marketplace, and keeping thousands of SKUs accurate. CommerceClarity replaces that manual work with AI agents.
As a Retail Engineer you put those agents to work inside each customer’s operation, from discovery and workflow design to integration and production. Part retail consultant, part engineer, working with our customers across the UK.
This is a high-ownership seat. You own our most strategic accounts end to end and you set the delivery method the rest of the team runs on. We weigh attitude and the combination over years on paper: the sweet spot is three to six years, and the right builder energy beats seniority.
This is one of the first seats we are opening in the UK. You would work out of the London hub on UK accounts, with the platform and the delivery method already built behind you in Milan and Barcelona.
## A job that did not exist three years ago
New tools tend to produce job titles that were not there a few years earlier. Growth engineer and marketing engineer both appeared once the people who understood the funnel could write the code that ran it, and forward deployed engineer appeared when the same thing happened to enterprise delivery. None of the three was a rename. They exist because splitting the person who understands the process from the person who builds it stopped paying for itself.
Retail Engineer is that title for catalog operations. Most of the people who fit it have spent five or six years in solution consulting or solution delivery at a retail software vendor or a consultancy. They read business processes for a living and they own the customer, and almost all of them have a technical side they were never given room to use: the configuration screen ended exactly where the interesting part started, and everything past it went to a development team on another continent.
What changed is the platform. The agents are built there, changed there and run there, so the person who designs the workflow is the person who builds it, in front of the customer, in the same week. You write the prompts and you wire up their systems, and when a number moves you go and change whatever produced it. AI coding assistants work alongside you, so a change that used to take a sprint becomes a prompt and a test.
The half of the job you were already good at stays. Discovery, a room full of stakeholders, an account that trusts you: here that is what keeps the building honest, because you are the one who heard what they actually meant. What you gain is the other half. You spend your days on agent design, evals and prompt engineering, inside a company that runs its own operations on agents, which is a faster education in this than anything you could sign up for.
## Why this role is different
It is not pure delivery and it is not pure engineering. You sit at the intersection: you understand the retailer’s catalog workflow well enough to redesign it around agents, and you have the depth to build the agent flows yourself.
You cover the whole lifecycle. The preparation, mapping their processes, designing the workflow, writing and iterating the prompts, defining the KPIs. Then the run, deployment, integration with their systems, monitoring, debugging, and optimization against those KPIs.
And you do not only deliver. You shape how we deliver and you grow the engineers around you, so one senior hire lifts the team instead of adding a pair of hands. You work closely with the Agent Product Managers, who own the product direction, and with the AI Engineers on delivery.
## What you would do
* Lead agent implementations end to end for enterprise retailers, from kickoff to production, on our DIPE method: design, implement, prove, evolve.
* Own our most strategic accounts and the heaviest proofs of concept directly.
* Define the success KPIs with the customer, and build the measurement loop that proves the agents are working.
* Design and build the agent workflows, and write the prompt layer that drives them.
* Integrate agents with customer systems: PIM, ERP, ecommerce platforms, marketplaces, data warehouses.
* Own the run. Monitor, debug, iterate on prompts and flows, and move the numbers over time.
* Structure how we deliver, and grow the engineers around you, so the team scales on method instead of drowning.
* Feed what you learn back into the product and the agent roadmap.
## What we are looking for
### Essential
* Three or more years of experience, most of it in consulting or solution delivery. Many of our best fits are management engineers who read a business process and enjoy working with data.
* You sit between business and technology. You can redesign a retailer’s catalog workflow and build the agent flow yourself. Not a pure PM, not a pure data engineer.
* Prompt engineering sense. You iterate against real data, you measure output quality, and you know when to fix something with a prompt and when to fix it with code.
* Standing with enterprise customers, and a record of bringing complex delivery home.
* You have managed projects and people, and you still want to build rather than only coordinate.
* Customer-facing and high agency. You handle ambiguity, you lead the conversation with the retailer, and you do not wait for a perfect brief.
* English to native standard, and you are at home in the UK market. Italian is a plus.
### Preferred
* Hands-on with workflow builders such as n8n, and with AI-native coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex.
* Comfortable coding with AI assistance, in Python or TypeScript, to glue systems together and extend what an agent does.
* You have worked with a workflow orchestration engine.
* Deep retail workflow knowledge: catalog management, PIM, assortment, attribute governance, channel publishing, marketplace operations.
* The major PIM platforms, Akeneo, Salsify, inRiver, Pimcore, and the feed and channel managers.
* A background as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Implementation Lead or technical CSM at an enterprise software company.
* Retail data quality at scale: millions of SKUs, many languages, many marketplaces.
## The team you would join
Our founders have spent their careers building and operating retail at scale. They have founded retail companies generating tens of millions in revenue, launched and scaled Amazon’s operations in Italy and Spain, led operations at Everli across more than 2,000 employees, and shaped product direction at Shopify and Zalando. Operator, founder, product leader. Every seat that defined modern European commerce.
## What we offer
* Ownership. Your work reaches production and customers fast, and shapes the delivery method directly.
* Growth. A high-leverage team, real commercial complexity, tight feedback loops.
* An ambitious roadmap. Help define the operating infrastructure for agentic commerce in Europe.
* A new craft. You learn to build and ship with agents and AI coding assistants, and it compounds.
* Flexible hybrid. The London hub, three days a week minimum, plus four remote weeks a year.

### Position Overview
We are looking for a talented Advanced Human Factors Engineer to join our growing team. Being part of the Human Factors and Usability team, you will be involved in planning, running and delivering a range of exciting human factors projects across all phases of development. You will be working with both internal project teams and global medical clients on developing safe and usable medical devices, ensuring that user needs are considered early and often throughout the design process. You will be responsible for identifying user needs and supporting use-related risk mitigation through the application of Human Factors principles and best practice.
The role involves a range of activities such as desk and field research, use-related risk management, planning and conducting Human Factors studies and compiling results into clear and concise reports appropriate for client teams and in accordance to regulatory standards.
Check out what our Human Factors team is all about: Crux - Human Factors
**Why us?**
* Work with top pharma clients on cutting-edge medical device projects.
* Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team across our Bristol (UK) and Boston (US) offices.
* Travel opportunities to support global project delivery.
* Influence the development of life-changing healthcare technologies.
* Be part of a consultancy that values curiosity, integrity, and collaboration.
### Principal Responsibilities
* Accurate planning and timely delivery of usability and Human Factors activities.
* Ensuring user needs are identified and met through the integration of usability in product development.
* Analysing data to generate tangible and feasible design solutions that improve the usability and reduce use-related risk.
* Liaising with external suppliers to enable efficient execution of Human Factors studies.
* Producing clear, concise written reports and presentations.
* Formulating and executing of a design and usability strategy to meet client objectives.
* As a subject matter expert, presenting ideas to colleagues and clients with varying levels of technical knowledge, questioning where appropriate to ensure impactful output and being persuasive and able to 'sell' your ideas to others.
* Promoting awareness of usability within the business and helping to promote Crux’s growing in-house Human factors capabilities by proactively developing knowledge of relevant regulations, processes and best practice.
* Building trusted relationships within existing client accounts and pursuing opportunities and referrals for selling usability services into these accounts.
* Preparing and advising on small quotes.
* Support Crux’s continual development, improving processes and procedures.
### What We’re Looking For
**Essential**:
* Experience of applying a range of Human Factors techniques and usability principles.
* In-depth understanding of Human Factors guidance documents and standards for medical device development.
* Experience in evaluating and improving designs based on sound usability understanding.
* Skilled and experienced in moderating varied user research and putting participants at ease.
* Experience in data capture and analysis.
* A proven ability to synthetise a lot of information and distil it into meaningful design recommendations.
* Strong report writing skills.
* Excellent presentation and interpersonal communication skills.
* Exceptional planning and organisational skills.
* Ability to work cooperatively and dependably as part of a team or independently.
* Great attention to detail.
* An understanding of up-to-date regulatory frameworks surrounding medical device development, including IEC62366 and FDA Human Factors regulations.
* Flexible and accommodating work ethic.
* Achieved a first or high 2:1 classification in a relevant accredited degree program.
* Due to the nature of this role, appointment is subject to a Basic DBS check.
**Desirable**:
* Experience in a consultancy environment for the medical, pharma or health industries.
* Working towards CIEHF chartership
### Why you'll love working here
We’re a dynamic, fast‐growing engineering consultancy with a reputation for delivering brilliant work and for being a genuinely great place to build your career.
Our benefits package is designed to support your wellbeing and work-life balance. You’ll enjoy a generous holiday allowance, life assurance, a generous pension scheme, bike‐to‐work options, a health cash plan, enhanced family leave and opportunities to get involved in social events throughout the year.

**Principal Clinical Scientist**
*(Senior Clinical Scientist level also considered)*
**The Role**
We're looking for a clinical scientist — someone who has been the scientific lead for clinical studies before, from protocol development to start-up (development of critical study documents) through to study execution, data analysis and interpretation and close-out with a clinical study report. Having prepared regulatory submissions of study results is a pre. You'll work in close partnership with the clinical operations team and CROs under the team's full-outsource operating model, managing that day-to-day relationship rather than delivering trial activity in-house. It's one of two newly approved roles, created ahead of anticipated demand rather than to backfill a departure, which means there's genuine room to help shape how the team works rather than simply joining an existing structure.
*Hybrid based (3 days a week onsite) in Maidenhead (UK), Melbourne (Aus) or Zurich (CH)*
**Why It Matters**
A clinical study is only as good as the people running it. A weak protocol, poorly managed start-up, or a fumbled relationship with the CRO delivering the trial can cost a program months — sometimes far more — and that delay sits between a therapy and the patients waiting on it. This role exists because CSL is adding capacity to get that execution right: someone who can lead all scientific needs of a study properly, and co-own the end to end alongside clinical operations, is what actually moves a clinical development plan forward. It's not a supporting or administrative function — it's the core that determines whether the science translates into a trial that runs cleanly and data that holds up.
**What You'll Be Responsible For**
You'll take ownership of clinical studies end-to-end, acting as the scientific and operational anchor between the program team and outsourced delivery partners.
* Lead all scientific elements of clinical studies from protocol development through study execution to a final clinical study report
* Write and/or take responsibility for study protocols, clinical study reports and other critical study documents
* Manage, alongside the clinical operations lead, day-to-day working relationships with CROs under a full-outsource operating model
* Collaborate closely with the cross-functional study teams — this is a collaborative role, not an isolated one one
* Contribute to the scientific interpretation of clinical data and supporting documentation
* Build working relationships across the wider team, including colleagues based in the US and Australia
**Experience Required**
* Demonstrated, hands-on experience with clinical studies (protocol development, execution, close-out) — not solely oversight or academic exposure
* Experience writing clinical study protocols and clinical study reports directly
* Experience working within a full-outsource / CRO-dependent operating model
* A collaborative, cross-functional working style — comfortable building relationships rather than working independently

CSL Seqirus is part of CSL. As one of the largest influenza vaccine providers in the world, CSL Seqirus is a major contributor to the prevention of influenza globally and a transcontinental partner in pandemic preparedness. With state-of-the-art production facilities in the U.S., the U.K. and Australia, CSL Seqirus utilizes egg, cell and adjuvant technologies to offer a broad portfolio of differentiated influenza vaccines in more than 20 countries around the world.

* At least 5 years’ project management experience in AV, construction or technical delivery.
* Extensive knowledge of AV technologies and systems integration processes.
* A structured, proactive way of working with excellent planning, prioritisation and attention to detail, comfortable managing a demanding, multi-project workload to strict deadlines.
* Strong commercial awareness, with the ability to create, read and negotiate contracts, schedules, budgets and project plans.
* Highly numerate and comfortable working with complex data
* Excellent written and verbal communication in fluent English, with the confidence to be assertive when needed and to explain technical requirements clearly to non-technical audiences.
* Knowledge of construction management and experience working with general contractors, architects and electrical contractors.
* The ability to read, comprehend and redline CAD packages.
* Strong IT skills: Excel, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint.

Own project requirements and objectives end to end: financial, technical, programme, construction and production coordination, materials, personnel and scopes of work.

The Cloud Security Engineer role is designed for a hands-on security specialist with broad Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 experience who can implement, harden and assure cloud security controls. Candidates may have progressed through cloud engineering, infrastructure, identity and access management, security operations or consultancy roles and will be comfortable working directly in client environments.
The role supports a varied portfolio of predominantly Azure security work spanning identity and privileged access, platform governance, networking, workload protection, secrets and encryption, logging and monitoring, data protection and automation. Strong practical experience with Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management and wider Privileged Access Management capabilities is particularly valued, alongside experience with Microsoft Purview across information protection, data classification and data loss prevention.
This is not an exclusively identity or data-security role. The successful candidate will be expected to apply their core areas of expertise while developing and maintaining capability across the wider Azure and Microsoft 365 security landscape.
Sitting within Cyro’s Cyber Security Architecture team, the successful candidate will work closely with security architects to translate security requirements and High-Level Designs into detailed, implementable solutions. They will own Low-Level Designs, build documentation and engineering delivery, while contributing to High-Level Designs, reference architectures and reusable security patterns. The role provides a clear development path towards security architecture for candidates with the aptitude and ambition to progress in that direction.
### Primary responsibilities:
#### Azure Security Engineering:
* Implement, configure, harden and troubleshoot security controls across Azure and Microsoft 365 environments.
* Configure Microsoft Entra ID controls including Conditional Access, multi-factor authentication, role-based access control, managed identities, access reviews and identity lifecycle controls, with particular emphasis on Privileged Identity Management and the application of appropriate privileged access controls.
* Implement platform governance using management groups, subscriptions, landing zone controls, Azure Policy and initiatives, Defender for Cloud, secure score and regulatory compliance capabilities.
* Engineer network security controls including virtual networks, network security groups, Azure Firewall, web application firewall, Private Link and private endpoints, DNS security, DDoS protection and hybrid connectivity controls.
* Implement Key Vault, encryption, secret and certificate management, secure storage patterns and workload identity controls.
* Secure Azure workloads including virtual machines, containers and AKS, App Service, Functions, storage, databases and other platform services.
* Configure security logging and monitoring using Azure Monitor, Log Analytics and Microsoft Sentinel, and integrate relevant Defender XDR telemetry.
* Implement Microsoft Purview capabilities where required, including information protection, sensitivity labels, data classification, data loss prevention, retention and records controls.

#### Automation and DevSecOps:
* Build and maintain secure, repeatable deployments using Bicep, Terraform, PowerShell, Azure CLI or equivalent infrastructure-as-code and automation tooling.
* Integrate security guardrails, policy-as-code, secrets handling and security testing into Azure DevOps or GitHub-based delivery pipelines.
* Develop scripts, reusable modules and operational runbooks that improve consistency, supportability and delivery efficiency.
#### Design, Assurance and Documentation:
* Gather technical requirements, contribute to HLDs and own LLDs, build guides, configuration standards, test plans, runbooks and as-built documentation, progressively taking on greater design responsibility with support from experienced security architects.
* Perform cloud security configuration reviews and hardening assessments against Microsoft security guidance, CIS benchmarks, the NCSC CAF, ISO 27001 and client standards.
* Test changes, remediate findings and provide implementation assurance and operational handover to client and managed service teams.
#### client and team engagement:
* Lead defined engineering work packages under general direction, planning activity, managing dependencies and maintaining delivery quality.
* Work directly with client architects, engineers, service teams and stakeholders to explain implementation choices, risks and operational impacts.
* Support technical discovery, estimates, proposals and client demonstrations, and contribute to reusable patterns and the development of Cyro's cloud security services.
### Essential skills and experience:
* Strong hands-on experience engineering and securing Microsoft Azure environments.
* Practical capability across several Azure security domains, including identity, governance, networking, workload protection, logging and secrets management.
* Experience with Microsoft Entra ID, including practical exposure to Privileged Identity Management, together with experience across a selection of Azure security technologies such as Azure Policy, Defender for Cloud, Key Vault, Azure Monitor and Log Analytics.
* Experience using infrastructure-as-code or scripting tools such as Bicep, Terraform, PowerShell or Azure CLI.
* Ability to interpret architectural requirements and translate HLDs into accurate LLDs, build documentation, test plans and operational runbooks.
* Strong troubleshooting skills and experience resolving cloud configuration, access, policy and integration issues.
* Understanding of cloud security principles including least privilege, defence in depth, secure-by-design, segmentation, encryption and continuous monitoring.
* Good client-facing communication, documentation and stakeholder engagement skills.
* Ability to work autonomously under general direction, lead defined work packages and guide colleagues where appropriate.
* Eligibility for UK Security Clearance (successful appointment will be subject to being granted Security Clearance).
* Willingness to work across a varied portfolio of cloud security engineering activities, applying existing strengths while developing capability in other areas.
### desirable Skills and Experience:
* Hands-on experience with Microsoft Purview, particularly Information Protection, sensitivity labels, data classification or data loss prevention.
* Microsoft certifications such as AZ-500, AZ-104, SC-300, SC-400 or SC-100.
* Experience with Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR or Defender for Cloud Apps.
* Experience implementing security controls through Azure DevOps or GitHub CI/CD pipelines.
* Knowledge of the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark, CIS Azure benchmarks, the NCSC CAF, ISO 27001 or NIST guidance.
* Experience securing hybrid environments or familiarity with AWS or GCP security controls.
* Exposure to security design or architecture activities, or a demonstrable interest in developing towards a security architecture role.
* Experience working in or with Critical National Infrastructure, UK Government or similarly regulated environments.

#### Position
*This role is offered on a UK employment contract. Candidates must be based in the UK as we are unable to support remote working from outside the country due to local employment and tax legislation.*
**Position**
This role sits within Deltatre's Engineering & Technology function, reporting to the SVP of Engineering Delivery, at the interface between external and internal clients and the multi-disciplinary teams building and running the OTT streaming and connected consumer experiences for major international sports and entertainment brands.
As Technical Delivery Director, you hold delivery accountability for a portfolio of programmes - directing delivery leadership while staying personally credible in the architecture conversation, and personally present when a client escalation matters. You own end-to-end delivery against customer needs, while ensuring engineering squads' contribution to the core product meets Deltatre's standards for quality. This is a delivery-focused leadership role, not a hands-on coding one: you'll be judged on delivery outcomes and squad health, coordinating the team rather than writing the code yourself. Alongside other technical principals, you lead architectural decisions within the agreed architecture, drive requirements gathering and estimation, and combine your engineering background with the leadership and mentoring that scale a team's standards over time.
You'll take initial ownership of 6 delivery squads (around 40-45 engineers), with the 6 squad leads reporting directly to you. This is an expansion-oriented role: as the team and business grow, the remit may extend further, though nothing beyond the current scope is confirmed at this stage.
**Responsibilities**
**End-to-end delivery ownership**
* Own the delivery of client programmes end to end - requirements, defining buildable scope, managing delivery forecasts, managing launch and release, and ongoing project run
* Report exact delivery status across all reporting squads and external dependencies
* Maintain high standards of technical delivery, including code contribution processes, Definition of Ready, and Definition of Done
**Squad and team leadership**
* Take ownership of 6 delivery squads (around 40-45 engineers) initially, with the 6 squad leads reporting directly to you, setting day-to-day direction and priorities and removing whatever is blocking them
* Manage team delivery capacity and key-person risk, forecasting any shortfalls and making the case for additional squad capacity from internal or external teams
* Maintain a high standard of engineering across squads - review output, mentor engineers, and lead by example
**Governance and stakeholder management**
* Own governance practices and collaboration spanning Delivery Directors and Project Managers assigned to client programmes, with effective liaison into Product Management
* Build and maintain technical relationships with clients
* Know when to escalate, and stay proactive in delivery problem-solving
#### Requirements
You have done this before - here's what we're looking for.
**Required**
* 10+ years' experience in software engineering, ideally including Java, React Native, or JavaScript/TypeScript - a mandatory technical foundation that lets you genuinely understand what your squads are building, even though this role is delivery-focused rather than hands-on coding day to day
* Delivery accountability for a portfolio of concurrent large-scale programmes, ideally in OTT/streaming, media technology, a product organisation, or a strong technical consultancy
* Demonstrable experience leading through other technical and delivery leaders, and developing them
* Solution architecture experience across a mix of digital platforms
* Senior client-facing credibility, able to manage fixed-date escalations and negotiate scope while maintaining trusted relationships
* Commitment to managing commercial consequences - negotiating and planning for margin, penalty exposure, fixed-price versus T&M, and supplier mix
* Track record of working alongside a technical-authority peer while keeping boundaries intact
* Agile delivery in practice, adapted to fixed-date commitments rather than argued with
* Documentation and decision discipline - auditable records of decisions and the reasoning behind them
**Valued**
* Multi-tenant platform or productised-services experience, working with a shared codebase
* Experience building a delivery function through significant scale-up, including hiring and onboarding at volume
* Distributed and offshore delivery experience across regions and time zones
* Product management experience
* Familiarity with multiple delivery methodologies, with the judgement to choose the right pattern for the job at hand
* Background in OTT, VOD, live broadcast, or media technology
**Who Thrives Here**
This role carries accountability at the portfolio level, not the project level - you're moving between a squad's blockers, a client escalation, and a margin conversation in the same day, and each needs your full attention and judgement. It suits someone who stays technically credible without staying purely hands-on, and who can hold a boundary with a technical-authority peer without it becoming a turf war.
People who do well here treat documentation and decision discipline as protection for the whole programme, not overhead, and they know the difference between a problem to solve quietly and one that needs to be escalated now. You'll need the client-facing weight to negotiate scope under pressure and the internal credibility to lead delivery leaders who don't report to you directly.
**Process and what to expect**
* Introductory conversation: a step for us to get to know each other better, and for us to answer all questions you might have around Deltatre.
* 1-hour Technical round of Interview: we will deep dive on your experience and explore the technical and architectural decisions you have made in your past work.
* 1-hour Competency Based Interview: we will ask you situational questions around how you deal with real-life scenarios at work. Easier doing it, more than explaining it.
If any of these formats would be difficult for you, tell us - we adjust regularly and can usually accommodate.
*Accessibility and accommodation questions are welcome at any stage. Tell us what would work for you.*

# Senior Integration & Automation Engineer
**About the Devonshire Group**
The Devonshire Group comprises the Devonshire family interests, charities and businesses throughout the UK and Ireland, including Chatsworth in Derbyshire, the Bolton Abbey Estate in North Yorkshire, the Lismore Estate in County Waterford, and the Compton Estate in Sussex.
# Across our estates and businesses, we operate visitor attractions, shops, restaurants and luxury accommodation, alongside tenanted residential and commercial property, farming and forestry enterprises, and a significant property development pipeline. We employ around 1,400 colleagues across more than 65,000 acres.
# We are committed to benefitting heritage, people and a shared future, preserving and enhancing our heritage assets, supporting our communities, and leading by example in how we do things.
