# About hyperexponential (hx)
At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.
Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.
Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.
What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.
What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.
If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.
# **About the team**
Finance at hx is a lean, AI-native team that builds the operational engine behind a high-growth, fast-moving business. The team's job is to turn complexity into clarity: giving leaders accurate numbers, clean controls, and the confidence to make bold decisions quickly. It is not a back-office function; it is close to the action, involved early in decisions, and expected to shape how the business scales.
The team is still building its foundations, which means there is genuine scope to define how processes work, not just execute them. Everyone on the team is relatively new to their role, and that is by design. hx is growing quickly, and the Finance function is scaling to match. What that means in practice is that the people who join now have the opportunity to build things from scratch, automate what should not be done by hand, and become a cornerstone of how the company operates for years to come.
This role sits at the heart of day-to-day finance operations: revenue, VAT, payroll, banking, and month-end close. The work is precise, deadline-driven, and consequential. If you find satisfaction in owning a process properly, keeping it clean, and making it better over time, this is the environment where that instinct will be rewarded.
**Check out our** **Finance Candidate Hub** **for a behind the scenes look at the team you would be joining!**
# **What you'll be doing**
* Own the end-to-end revenue and accounts receivable cycle in NetSuite, ensuring sales orders are raised promptly, invoices reflect the correct FRS102 revenue recognition treatment, and the AR ledger is reconciled monthly with no unexplained misstatements at year-end audit.
* Drive the month-end close to a defined timetable, completing the close by working day four and ensuring all balance sheet reconciliations are evidenced and reviewed by working day seven.
* Manage UK VAT compliance from preparation through to filing, maintaining audit-ready workpapers at all times and ensuring every return is reconciled, accurate, and submitted on time with no penalties.
* Take full ownership of UK payroll once the HiBob transition completes, processing each monthly run accurately and on schedule, and maintaining clean payroll-to-NetSuite reconciliations.
* Oversee banking, treasury, and payment controls, including maintaining a rolling cash flow forecast, keeping bank accounts reconciled in NetSuite, and acting as a control point on payment runs to prevent unauthorised or duplicate payments.
* Identify and deliver at least one process improvement or automation each quarter, keeping SOPs current and approaching documentation as a control rather than an administrative task.
# **What you'll need to have done**
* Operated core finance processes end-to-end in a fast-paced or high-growth environment, with clear personal ownership of recurring cycles such as revenue, VAT, payroll, or month-end close rather than supporting a larger team at arm's length.
* Used NetSuite hands-on across multiple functional areas, including Advanced Revenue Management, intercompany transactions, and reconciliation workflows; experience across more than one organisation or configuration is a strong advantage. NetSuite experience is a prerequisite for this role. You must be able to demonstrate what your day to day use and experience is, and how you have driven optimisation of NetSuite.
* Prepared and filed UK VAT returns with a solid understanding of coding, reconciliation, and the treatment of non-UK sales and purchases, and maintained documentation to a standard that can withstand an HMRC query without a handover.
* Taken meaningful responsibility for a month-end close process, including understanding the full sequence of steps, managing to a timetable, and identifying where controls or documentation needed strengthening.
* Demonstrated a consistent instinct for improving and automating manual processes, with the ability to articulate both the before and the after, and the judgement to know when a manual control should be kept.
* Shown the character and values that make finance work in a high-trust environment: honesty about problems before they escalate, clear written communication, and a collaborative mindset that strengthens the team around you.
# **You're unlikely to thrive here if**
* You prefer stability and predictability over environments where processes are still being built and priorities can shift quickly.
* You are most comfortable contributing to a defined part of a process rather than owning the outcome end-to-end and taking responsibility when something is not right.
* You see documentation and SOPs as administrative overhead rather than a meaningful part of doing the job well.
If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.
# **Compensation**
At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.
Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.
Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this.

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.
25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).
Company pension scheme via Penfold.
Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.
Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).
Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.
Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry
Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

hxer's are at the centre of everything we build. If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

* Ability to work in a fast-paced, multi-regional environment.

You schedule it, release it to the floor, and follow it through stores, production and dispatch until it is on a truck and invoiced. The split is deliberate. At our scale planning and buying are each a full time job, and neither gets the attention it deserves when one person does both.
The line between the two roles is simple. The Buyer owns the supplier: selection, price, terms, contract and performance. You own the schedule and the movement, internally and externally, including materials and subcontract processes. They agree the deal, you call it off.
Be clear about what you are walking into. We have an MRP system that is not yet doing the work it should. Routings are not broken down far enough, work centre data is incomplete, and we find out about a capacity constraint when we are already inside it. Your first job is to make SYSPRO tell the truth. Your second is to run two factories from it. If that sounds like the part of the job you would enjoy most, this is the right role for you.
**What will you be doing?**
###### **Planning and scheduling**
• Enter customer sales orders, confirm that capacity and material support the promised delivery date, and raise it internally early with alternatives when they do not.
• Own the master production schedule for Gloucester and Swindon, sequencing work to make the best use of equipment, labour and tooling.
• Generate manufacturing works orders from MRP and make sure the optimal production method and routing is used when raising them.
• Issue the daily and weekly Work to List to Production at each site, then follow up on adherence rather than filing it.
• Load work centre capacity in MRP so constraints are visible weeks ahead. Flag where we need more capacity and where we have spare to fill.
• Run the MRP regeneration on a fixed cycle and action what it tells you.
• Plan around planned absence, shutdowns and maintenance windows rather than discovering them.
###### **Planning data integrity**
• Own the accuracy of the planning data in SYSPRO: routings, work centres, run and elapsed times, lead times, bills of material and stocking levels.
• Work with Manufacturing Engineering to get routings broken down into real operations. One line that says make part does not schedule a factory.
• Keep sales orders, part numbers and due dates loaded correctly and on time, so the order book is one source of truth for Operations, Finance and the management team.
• Be the operational voice in our ERP development. Bring the requirement, test the change, train the users, then hold people to using the system as designed.
###### **Inventory, stores and logistics**
• Own goods in. Receipt, scan, hand to inspection and book to stock on the day it lands.
• Own stores and kitting. Right material, right quantity, right job, issued at the right operation.
• Run location, warehouse and freezer discipline, including shelf life and out life control on refrigerated material.
• Hold inventory at the level that keeps the line running without tying up cash or creating waste. Recommend and maintain min, mid and max levels on purchased components.
• Own and optimise the vendor managed inventory process with the Buyer.
• Plan, execute and reconcile stock cycle counts at both sites, and keep work in progress booked accurately so stock records mean something.
• Schedule call offs and inbound deliveries against the agreements the Buyer has put in place, so material lands when the build needs it, not months early or a week late.
• Own the movement of parts through subcontract processes. Book the slot, get the parts out, track what is sitting at the subcontractor, and get them back on the date.
• Own dispatch and outbound logistics: packing, carriers, freight, delivery notes and export documentation, right first time.
• Move material between Gloucester and Swindon on a plan, not on a phone call.
###### **Control and reporting**
• Report weekly on schedule adherence, on time in full delivery, capacity load, labour utilisation, stock accuracy and shortages.
• Give early warning when a job is going to slip, with the reason and the recovery plan. A surprise at month end is a planning failure.
• Run a short weekly production review across both sites: what we committed, where we are, what is at risk, what we are doing about it.
• Work across Production, Engineering, Quality, Stores, Finance and Business Development so plans are aligned before they are committed, not after.
• Use our existing supply chain and operational processes, stay current on all activity, and keep the improvements coming.
• Other duties as the business demands. We are scaling, and this job will grow with us. Accountable to produce the MPS (master production schedule) driving cross functional accountability against commitments and linked in to the overall IBP (Integrated Business Plan)
**What do we need from you?**
###### **Essential**
• Proven production planning or scheduling experience in a manufacturing environment.
• Strong working knowledge of ERP / MRP planning and scheduling. Hands on, not theoretical. You can build a routing, set up a work centre and run MRP yourself.
• Solid understanding of manufacturing processes and how they translate into times, routings and capacity.
• Practical stores, stock control and inventory accuracy experience.
• Strong analytical and problem solving skills, and real comfort with data. You will build your own numbers and defend them.
• Accuracy under pressure. A wrong figure in MRP becomes a late part, and a late part becomes a customer call.
• The nerve to hold a plan against pressure from every direction, and to change it only for a reason.
• Clear, direct communication with Production, Engineering, Stores, Quality, Finance and customers.
• The ability to hold multiple priorities across two sites without losing the thread.
• Willingness to travel regularly between Gloucester and Swindon, and a full UK driving licence.
• A continuous improvement mindset and the appetite to build a broad knowledge of how we manufacture.
###### **Desirable**
• Experience with SYSPRO is a big advantage.
• Aerospace, automotive or defence manufacturing background.
• Experience cleaning up MRP data, routings, bills of material and work centres in a business where the system was not being used properly.
• Exposure to AS9100 or IATF 16949 quality management systems.
• Experience with shelf life and out life controlled material, including freezer stock.
• Dispatch and export documentation experience.
• APICS CPIM, or working towards it.
• Experience standing up planning processes in a business that is growing fast, rather than maintaining ones that already exist.
**Our Values: Uncompromising Excellence**
* **Discipline over excuses.** We commit. We follow through. We hold ourselves and each other to the highest standard, especially when the pressure is on.
* **Push the edge.** iCOMAT was built on a refusal to accept that curved fiber could not be manufactured at scale. We innovate where others hesitate.
* **Aligned and accountable.** Everyone owns their lane, communicates openly, and delivers without being chased. No silos. No ambiguity.
**Why iCOMAT?**

**You should be a hands-on platform engineer who builds through code and automates by default.** Your experience might centre on infrastructure as code, deployment pipelines, automation, platform tooling or service integrations. What matters is that you have built reliable, repeatable capabilities that engineering teams use to deliver and operate software.

We are hiring two Principal Platform Engineers to help unify authentication and authorisation across our next-generation enterprise software platform.
We are consolidating a fragmented authorisation landscape into one model across three hosting environments: our cloud-native platform, our legacy hosting platform and our lifecycle cloud. It must be correct, fast and reliable in distributed, multi-tenant environments.
Our current stack includes SpiceDB backed by PostgreSQL for authorisation, and Curity for authentication, with Keycloak estates migrating onto it. These describe the systems you will work on; prior experience with every product is not required.
You will design and build platform services, APIs and automation, own them in production, and establish patterns that product engineering teams can adopt confidently. A central part of the role is making secure authentication and authorisation available through documented, automated, self-service workflows.

* The ability to reason about correctness, latency, consistency and the traceability of authorisation decisions.
* Familiarity with fine-grained authorisation engines or policy-as-code approaches is valuable.

* Experience implementing or extending authentication flows in software, with an understanding of validation, trust boundaries and failure modes.
* Understanding of enterprise federation, SSO and external identity-provider integration in a customer-facing platform.
* Deeper experience engineering and operating authentication infrastructure at scale is particularly welcome.
**Production ownership**

* An approach to reliability that includes observability, performance testing, safe rollouts, rollback, backup and recovery.
* Examples of diagnosing production failures and using code or automation to prevent recurrence.
* Sound engineering judgement across distributed systems, relational data and event-driven services.

You will remain close to the code while helping other engineers make good architectural decisions. We value clear technical reasoning, constructive challenge and ownership from design through production.

* Strong coding and scripting skills applied to infrastructure, automation, deployment tooling or integrations. You should be comfortable maintaining code, reviewing changes and using automated tests.
* Experience automating provisioning, configuration, deployment and operational tasks through version-controlled, repeatable workflows.

AI Evaluation & Benchmarking Engineer
Location: Remote (United Kingdom) Salary: £60,000–£75,000 DOE Contract: Full-time, 40 hours per week Employer: Intergral UK Reports to: Director of Engineering
You must already have the right to work in the UK, as we're unable to sponsor visas for this role.
About the Role
We're looking for an AI Evaluation & Benchmarking Engineer to determine how we measure the quality of OpsPilot, and to build the systems that do it.
More important than any individual technology is how you approach measurement. We're looking for someone who questions whether a system is actually achieving the outcome it was designed for, works out how to measure that objectively, and builds what's needed to keep measuring it as the product changes.
You'll have real autonomy over the technical approach. We set the goals and check in regularly, but the expertise on how to get there is yours — we're hiring you because we need someone who can take an ambiguous problem and deliver a working system without being handed the steps. This is a hands-on engineering role with no reports and no QA silo. Our engineering structure is flat: you'll report to the Director of Engineering and work alongside the other engineers as a peer.
This isn't a traditional QA role. You won't be manually testing tickets, acting as a release gatekeeper or simply checking whether features technically work.
About OpsPilot
OpsPilot is an AI-led observability platform helping engineering and operations teams move from monitoring data to evidence-backed operational understanding — so they can investigate problems faster and act with greater confidence.
Intergral has more than 20 years of experience in application performance and observability, with an established customer base built around FusionReactor. OpsPilot is expanding beyond its historic Java and ColdFusion roots into the wider observability market, supporting OpenTelemetry-based metrics, logs and traces.
At the heart of OpsPilot is Coworker, an AI operations capability that continuously investigates telemetry, identifies situations that need attention and provides evidence-backed findings and recommended next steps.
What You'll Do
Evaluate the agent and the product it runs on
Coworker's findings are only as good as the system underneath them. An investigation can fail because the model reasoned badly, because retrieval surfaced the wrong evidence, because ingestion dropped a trace, or because the finding was presented in a way no engineer could act on. Evaluating the agent in isolation would tell us very little, so this role covers both.
On the agentic side, you'll:
* Build automated evaluations for our agentic AI capabilities.
* Create realistic synthetic scenarios, datasets and workloads with meaningful ground truth and evaluation criteria.
* Measure task success, diagnostic accuracy, evidence quality, reliability, consistency, latency and cost.
* Account for the non-deterministic nature of AI systems through repeated runs, variance analysis and determining whether changes are meaningful rather than noise.
* Benchmark models, prompts, tools, retrieval strategies and agent workflows against repeatable baselines.
* Use relevant industry benchmarks and standards, including established SRE practices and emerging AI-agent, AIOps and incident-response benchmarks, and build our own where existing approaches don't represent real operational work.
Across the wider product, you'll:
* Extend evaluation across important customer journeys, APIs, backend services and UI.
* Use OpenTelemetry, including its Semantic Conventions, to make benchmark environments representative and portable.
* Use product telemetry and correlate benchmark results with metrics, logs and traces to understand why failures occur.
* Build end-to-end measurements focused on customer outcomes rather than isolated components.
When we change a model, prompt, tool or agent workflow, we want to know what became better, what became worse and why — including the impact on quality, reliability, latency and cost.
Turn what we learn into continuous improvement
* Turn failures and real-world problems into new evaluation scenarios.
* Identify recurring failure patterns and capability gaps.
* Test potential improvements against established baselines, holdouts and unseen scenarios.
* Detect regressions, benchmark overfitting and improvements that don't generalise.
Longer term, this evaluation system becomes the harness for controlled self-improvement: identifying weaknesses, testing potential changes and objectively determining whether they should be retained. That's the direction of travel rather than the first year's work, but it's why we're building this properly.
Work with the rest of engineering
* Work directly with AI, software, platform and SRE engineers to investigate findings and improve the product.
* Make evaluation failures clear, reproducible and actionable.
* Make straightforward fixes yourself where that's the most efficient approach.
* Build tooling that makes evaluations easy for other engineers to create, run and understand.
* Use AI-assisted engineering where it improves the speed or quality of your work.
Benchmarking should provide continuous feedback that helps engineering improve the product. This role is not a release gatekeeper.
What We're Looking For
Above everything else: the ability to take an ambiguous technical problem, develop an approach and deliver a working system independently.
We're more interested in demonstrated ability than an exact number of years, but we'd generally expect around 3+ years of relevant technical experience. Your background might be as an AI engineer, software engineer, SRE, platform engineer, performance engineer, SDET or similar.
Alongside that, we're looking for:
* Practical experience working with LLMs, AI agents or AI evaluation.
* Strong software engineering skills, particularly Python or a similar language.
* Experience building automated evaluation, benchmarking, testing or experimentation infrastructure.
* Experience creating synthetic workloads, datasets or evaluation scenarios.
* An understanding of non-deterministic evaluation, including repeated measurement, variance and distinguishing meaningful changes from noise.
* The ability to turn complex system behaviour into measurable criteria.
* Comfort working across APIs, distributed systems and multiple layers of a software product.
Desirable
Any of the following would be useful, but none are required:
* Agentic AI evaluation, tool use and multi-step workflows.
* LLM evaluation frameworks and model-based evaluation techniques.
* Automated experimentation or self-improving systems.
* Dataset, ground-truth and holdout evaluation design.
* Statistical experimentation and performance benchmarking.
* OpenTelemetry, metrics, logs and distributed tracing.
* SRE, incident response or observability.
* Production SaaS and distributed systems.
What Success Looks Like
We have the beginnings of an evaluation harness, but the design and expertise are what we're hiring for.
We'd expect the first few months to go into the core evaluation harness and a starting corpus for Coworker's investigation quality, then extend outward across the rest of the product as that proves itself. How you sequence it is your call.
By six months, we should be able to objectively answer questions such as:
* Is Coworker getting better at investigating operational problems?
* Where does it perform well or poorly, and why?
* Are its conclusions supported by the right evidence?
* How do different models, tools and agent configurations compare?
* What quality, latency and cost trade-offs are we making?
* How do we compare against relevant external benchmarks?
* Have improvements introduced regressions elsewhere?
* Where should we focus improvement next?
Our evaluation corpus should keep growing as we encounter new problems.
Success isn't measured by the number of tests written or percentage test coverage. It's measured by our ability to understand how well OpsPilot is doing its job, where it isn't, and whether the changes we're making are actually making it better.
What We Offer
A small company rather than a large one, with the trade-offs that implies. Under ten people in engineering, a flat structure, and decisions made in a conversation rather than across three meetings. You'll have genuine influence over how this is done, and very little bureaucracy to work through to get there.
* Fully remote within the UK.
* Flexible working hours.
* 25 days holiday plus bank holidays.

# Corporate Finance/M&A Analyst
**Corporate Finance/M&A Analyst**
This is a rare opportunity to join a small, high-impact Corporate Finance team and play a central part in Isio’s growth story. Working closely with the Head of Corporate Finance, you will gain hands-on exposure across the full deal lifecycle – from identifying targets and building the models that shape our decisions, through diligence, execution and integration. You will also have regular exposure to senior leadership, including the Group CFO and wider leadership team, and to our private equity investors.
It is a genuinely broad role for someone early in their career who wants to build deep M&A and corporate finance expertise, take on real responsibility quickly, and be part of a private-equity-backed growth story.
**What does the role entail?**
The Corporate Finance / M&A Analyst will support the Head of Corporate Finance in delivering Isio’s inorganic growth agenda across its core pensions businesses (pensions consulting and administration) and its diversification businesses (currently Wealth, Investments and Employee Benefits), as well as supporting organic growth through talent acquisition and team-lift modelling.
The role provides hands-on analytical and execution support across the full M&A lifecycle – from market scanning and target identification through to financial modelling, due diligence and integration. It also carries broader corporate finance responsibilities, including supporting the group’s capital structure through debt facility modelling and the tracking and reporting of management incentive schemes.
**Market Scanning, Target Identification & Pipeline Management**
· Conduct market scans across Isio’s core and diversification sectors to identify acquisition targets, team lifts and emerging opportunities.
· Build and maintain a target pipeline, tracking key metrics, strategic fit and engagement status.
· Research market trends, competitor activity and regulatory developments to inform target selection.
**Strategic Support**
· Support business unit leaders on their M&A strategy – exploring and challenging options, and developing the strategic rationale for prospective acquisitions.
· Contribute analysis and ideas to support capability-gap assessments across the business.
· Help prepare strategic insights and reports for senior leadership to inform investment, partnership and broader strategic decisions.
· Support organic growth through talent acquisition, including modelling the impact of team hires (“lifts”) on the business.
**Financial Modelling & Deal Evaluation**
· Build and maintain detailed financial models to assess valuation, returns and capital structure, including synergy and sensitivity analysis.
· Conduct financial, commercial and market due diligence in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
· Run scenarios and overlays that model the impact of acquisitions and team hires on group value, debt covenants, regulatory capital and shareholder returns, including analysis beyond the three-year horizon.
· Take ownership of the EBITDA metrics used in deal evaluation from initial modelling through to completion – ensuring diligence on EBITDA aligns with Isio’s accounting policies, and owning both the last-twelve-months EBITDA being acquired and the resulting run-rate EBITDA.
· Prepare outputs to support Investment Committee and Board decision-making.
**Transaction Execution**
· Help run M&A processes end-to-end, including timetables, workstream tracking and coordination across internal functions.
· Support due diligence, negotiation and documentation workstreams.
· Manage external advisers day-to-day, responding to queries and maintaining deal momentum.
**Post-Merger Integration**
· Support the development and tracking of integration plans and synergies for completed acquisitions.
**Capital Structure & Funding**
· Model the impact of M&A activity and other growth drivers, including team hires, on Isio’s debt and funding position.
· Partner with the Treasury and central finance teams to provide the M&A and growth inputs that feed the group’s funding and covenant analysis.
· Provide analysis on covenant headroom and funding capacity to inform deal structuring and Board decision-making.
· Support the tracking and reporting of management incentive schemes as part of the group’s capital structure.

· Newly qualified Chartered Accountant (or equivalent) from a Big Four or other leading accountancy practice, ideally with a few years post-qualification experience in transaction services, due diligence, M&A, investment banking, financial modelling and valuations, or a high-performing finance team.
· Candidates who are not qualified accountants but hold a degree in finance and/or accounting, with relevant experience, will also be considered.
· Strong financial modelling, valuation and analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex data into clear recommendations.
· Excellent commercial judgement and attention to detail.
· Confident written and verbal communication skills, comfortable engaging with senior stakeholders.
· A keen learner with a genuine desire to build a career in M&A, take on new challenges and be part of a private-equity-backed growth story.

We hold ourselves to the highest standards and our values guide how we advise our clients, how we operate as a business and how we work together as a team. We call it the *Isio Attitude.* We encourage our people to be bold, to communicate with conviction, and to deliver advice that matters.

Janus Henderson is undertaking a firm-wide AI transformation to become the most technologically sophisticated asset manager in the industry, and it has to move quickly without compromising security, resilience, or regulatory obligations. As Senior AI Platform Engineer, reporting to the Head of AI Technology, you will own the day-to-day engineering and lifecycle of that estate, from Azure AI Foundry and the AI model gateway through to Claude and our Copilot services. # Product Developer - Wearables
The KILLSTAR brand-universe is an invitation for people to explore, discover, and become who they are. We help affirm this invitation by creating an inclusive, supportive environment where our team members are embraced exactly as they are.
We are seeking a passionate individual with extensive experience in the full production lifecycle for creating clothing, footwear, and accessories. Reporting to our Product Development Manager, the ideal candidate will have a strong background in a commercial fashion environment, familiarity with industry best practices, and a solid understanding of working with critical paths.
In this role, you will collaborate with the wider design team on tasks such as creating tech packs, liaising with overseas manufacturers, cost engineering, troubleshooting production challenges, checking sample quality, and supporting the team during proto and sizing stages**.**
If this sounds like the opportunity for you - we would love to hear from you!
---
**WHAT YOU’LL DO:**
* Own the development of wearable ranges and products, including negotiating product costings and contributing ideas during range planning.
* Collaborate with Merchandising needs to facilitate and execute Design’s vision by sourcing brand-appropriate fabrics and trims, troubleshooting material, price, and delivery issues, and supporting overall business requirements.
* Maintain the fabric and trims library, supporting the development of raw materials and hardware.
* Share all new fabrics and trims with the Production and Compliance teams to ensure risk assessments and compliance testing are conducted as required.
* Assist in managing priorities during fit sessions, working in collaboration with the Technical Team.
* Liaise daily with factories, suppliers, and agents, managing and maintaining strong personal relationships with key suppliers.
* Own costing and negotiations for delegated categories and collections, including creating target costings, suggesting RRPs, and managing MOQs/projected volumes in partnership with the Merchandising Team.
* Understand target AUC and IMU, ensuring these are achieved for each category and collection, with a focus on consistent improvement.
* Create and review tech packs, collaborating with Design and Garment Technology, and finalising them before sharing with vendors for development.
* Manage the seasonal Critical Path and Buy Roll documents, regularly reviewing them with key stakeholders to implement improvements and updates.
* Update documents and trackers daily, ensuring accuracy and relevance.
* Work with the Technical Team to ensure the collection handover is completed in full and within the required timeline.
* Support other product ranges and areas as needed.
* Attend all handover and sign-off meetings, collaborating with teams to identify and address potential issues.
* Support and mentor junior team members, fostering growth and development.
---
**WHO YOU ARE:**
* **Analytical:** you can look at numbers all day, and help them make sense to others; you take a data-driven approach to problem solving and management.
* **An Agile Learner:** You learn quickly when something changes, you see failure as an opportunity, and you easily understand underlying structures and intentions.
* **Collaborative Negotiator:** you can negotiate skillfully in tough situations with both internal and external groups, settle differences with minimum noise, and win concessions while empowering relationships.
* **Detail Oriented:** you pride yourself on having every i dotted and every t crossed, never missing an important fact, figure, or detail.
* **Problem Solver:** you love simplifying complexity, discovering hidden answers, rooting out hidden problems, and finding solutions.
* **Organised:** you can orchestrate multiple activities at once to accomplish a goal, and marshal resources effectively to deliver results.
* **Solid Decision Maker:** Your solutions and suggestions are based on wisdom, critical thinking, experience, and sound judgement.
* **Reliable Communicator:** You are good about keeping people updated about changes, and your written and verbal communication is clear and concise.
---
**YOUR EXPERIENCE INCLUDES:**
* Previous experience as a Product Developer and/or Buyer, with a strong understanding of all stages of the production lifecycle and development process.
* Proficient in using Microsoft Office, with solid knowledge of Excel.
* Demonstrated experience working with critical paths, including identifying and resolving issues effectively.
* Skilled in providing clear feedback and outlining next steps to teams during the fit and sizing stages of production.
---
**BONUS IF YOU:**
* Have experience working with overseas factories and suppliers.
* Have experience of working on a variety of product categories: Apparel, Lifestyle, Homewear, Gifting etc.
* Have a personal affinity for the alternative community and fashion.
---
**WORK HOURS & LOCATION:**
Here at KILLSTAR, we support a hybrid working model. This means you will join us on site for three days a week at our HQ in Brighton. The other 2 days can be spent working from wherever you choose, either on-site, remotely or from home.
This role is a full-time position of 37.5 hours, with hours worked between 08:00am – 06:00pm, Monday through to Friday.
---

* Summer Fridays Early Finish
* YOU Day - one paid day off each year, just for you
* One paid volunteer day each year to support a charity or cause of your choice
* Flexible benefits platform designed around your wellbeing and personal preferences
* Employee Assistance Programme to offer support for personal or work-related issues aswell as financial and legal advice
* Staff Discount on all full-price items on our KILLSTAR site
* 5% Employer contributions to your pension
---

## About Us
Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar. Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes. 1,000+ customers across 50+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to **$100M+ in ARR**, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI and Graceview. We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law. Joining Legora means three things.
* We **lean in:** ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.
* We **fight for excellence:** high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.
* We **grow together:** as a team and with our customers.
Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.
If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.
**What you'll do**
Legal AI is inventing its best practices in real time, and this role sits where that happens. You'll sit within the Legal Engineering team and work hand in hand with Product at one of the fastest-growing legal AI companies in the world, seeing new capabilities before almost anyone else, experimenting with them against real legal work, and turning what you learn into the standards a global function runs on. In a year here, you will see and vet more legal AI use cases than most people in the industry see in a career, working directly with some of the best legal engineers in the industry.
This is a judgement role, not a filing one. You'll be the person who vets the skills, workflows and use cases the function ships: testing them hands-on, separating the genuinely strong from the merely plausible, and quality-controlling practice-area workflows so that what carries the Legora name is consistently excellent. You'll research and experiment with prompting techniques and applied AI methods, author the exemplar use cases the rest of the function copies, and teach what you learn: delivering technical onboarding for new Legal Engineers in your region and broadcasting best practices to the team worldwide. And because judgement needs grounding, around 30% of your time stays on live client work, chosen for what it teaches.
**Specifically, you will**
• Vet the Skills Library and Legal Engineering outputs against the quality bar: review skills, workflows and use cases hands-on before they go live, and quality-control practice-area workflows for consistency.
• Research and experiment with prompting techniques, skill patterns and emerging AI methods, and turn what works into best practices the whole function adopts.
• Author the reference use cases that show what great looks like, published as the exemplars others copy.
• Work closely with the Product team on up-and-coming capabilities: early hands-on testing, the first best practices for new features, and structured feedback from real use.
• Produce materials that would support the technical onboarding and training for new Legal Engineers in your region, such as best practices to create use cases etc.
• Communicate new best practices, exemplars and platform changes to the Legal Engineering team worldwide.
• Support the flagship demos our CEO and C-suite take on stage at the industry’s biggest events: use case preparation, fixtures and rehearsal support.
• Oversee the quality and currency of the use case and skills libraries, including coordination across regions
• Spend roughly 30% of your time on live client work, selected for what it feeds back into the standards and libraries.

**Senior Financial Analyst**
MAKO is putting shark skin on planes to save fuel and cut emissions.
Aviation burns roughly 100 billion gallons of fuel a year. Our riblet film makes aircraft slip through the air more cleanly, and every percent of drag we remove is fuel that never gets burned and CO2 that never gets emitted.
Turning a great technology into a real business takes funding, and a clear view of where it's going. That's where this role comes in. You'll help build MAKO's forward-looking view of our finances: budgets, forecasting, and modelling, and help teams across the business understand the financial impact of the decisions they're making. You'll report to our Senior Finance Manager.
**What You Will Do**
* **Manage the grant portfolio.** Monitor spend and budget-to-actuals, build budgets for new grant projects, contribute to grant reporting, and keep every dollar inside the guidelines
* **Make budgeting something teams actually use.** Partner with teams on annual and quarterly budgets, then run monthly budget-to-actual analysis and tell us plainly where the risks, the opportunities, and the savings are
* **Drive the runway view.** Prepare monthly cash flow forecasts and grow into broader forecasting and planning as the role develops
* **Power the big calls.** Use modelling and scenario analysis to help leadership choose between real options, with real numbers behind them
* **Build the tools.** Our reporting, dashboards, planning tools, and finance processes are yours to improve
**What Success Looks Like**
* **First month:** You know where the money is. You understand MAKO's financial position, our grants, our budgets, and how reporting works today. You've met the grant and budget owners across the business, and you can already name the gaps
* **First six months:** Our grants are tight: clear visibility over budgets, spend, remaining funding, and reporting deadlines. Budgeting and budget-to-actual processes are running reliably, and teams are genuinely managing their own numbers. Cash flow and runway forecasting is accurate, current, and something leadership actually leans on
* **First year:** People come to you before they make decisions, not after. Forecasting, planning, and management reporting have matured into a clear forward-looking view of performance, runway, risks, and opportunities, and your modelling is shaping commercial and strategic calls as we scale

* Qualified Chartered Accountant with experience in financial analysis, FP&A, management accounting, commercial finance, or similar

* Comfortable building things that don't exist yet
* Big-4, government grants, or R&D funding experience is a bonus, not essential
**Why You Should Join MAKO**
* **Impact**: Aviation is one of the hardest to abate industries, and its share of global emissions is only growing. Join our mission to improve the efficiency of the global fleet and save millions of tonnes of CO2 every year
* **Technology**: Our technology leverages the drag-reducing properties of shark skin to make aircraft more efficient. You'll be exposed to expertise and developments in materials, photolithography, fluid dynamics, and scale manufacturing

### Qui sommes-nous ?
Nous sommes à la pointe de la technologie mondiale en matière de soins de santé et nous nous attaquons avec audace aux problèmes de santé les plus difficiles auxquels l’humanité est confrontée en recherchant et en trouvant des solutions.

Nous sommes des ingénieurs dans l’âme et nous mettons en œuvre des idées ambitieuses pour trouver de véritables solutions pour des personnes bien réelles. Du laboratoire de R&D à l’usine, à la salle de conférence, tous nos collaborateurs expérimentent, créent, construisent, améliorent et cherchent des solutions. * **Vous connectez** à une culture dynamique et inclusive qui accepte de relever le défi de l’apprentissage tout au long de la vie

**Des expériences qui mettent les patients au premier plan.**Le respect des personnes est la marque de notre humanité. Cela permet à notre équipe d’avoir un impact positif sur ne serait-ce qu’une seule vie. **Location:** Liverpool
**Application deadline**: 11 January 2027 (Applications will only be reviewed once the deadline has passed)
**Entry requirements:** A 2:1 degree and at least 112 UCAS points from your top three subjects (or equivalent)
We're looking for talented individuals who bring initiative, creativity, and curiosity to the table. In return, you'll gain valuable hands-on experience, receive mentorship from some of the industry's best and earn recognised professional qualification.
By the end of your Graduate Programme, you’ll be a well-rounded, commercially minded professional, ready to take on interesting and challenging responsibilities. You won’t just be fully qualified - you’ll be fully prepared to drive your own career forward.
**What Sets Us Apart**
At MHA, people come first, our colleagues, our clients, and the communities we support. In 2026, we ranked as number 11 in the UK’s top accountancy firms and a proud member of Baker Tilly International, the world’s 8th largest network, we combine global insight with a strong local commitment.
Our people‐centred approach is what truly makes us different. You will be welcomed as a valued member of a collaborative, purpose‐led team. We are committed to continuous learning, growth, and creating an environment where everyone can thrive and be themselves.
We are proud to hold the Investors in People Gold award, recognising our commitment to supporting, developing, and valuing every individual.
**Here, You’ll Go Beyond Numbers**
We are looking for an Audit Junior to join us who is comfortable in an evolving environment and enjoys solving a variety of challenges that contribute to meaningful outcomes.
At MHA, you will be surrounded by passionate professionals who are committed to making a difference. Your work in Audit will go beyond the numbers, we believe in hands-on learning. You’ll be doing real work on real projects, not just shadowing. While you’ll receive mentorship and guidance, we prefer you to learn through extensive and practical on-the-job training.
Audit is a varied and highly client-facing career that gives you the opportunity to work with a wide range of organisations and understand how their businesses operate. You’ll spend time working at MHA offices as well as regularly travelling to and working from client sites, so you’ll need to be comfortable working in different environments, meeting new people and representing MHA professionally. As some client locations may be more difficult to reach by public transport, being able to travel independently and having access to a car can be beneficial for this role. From an early stage, you’ll build relationships with clients, ask questions and gather the information and evidence you need to support your work, while collaborating closely with colleagues across the audit team. You’ll develop your understanding of financial information and business processes, carry out testing and analytical work, and use your curiosity and professional judgement to explore anything that requires further attention. If you enjoy meeting new people, asking questions, understanding how businesses work and the variety of working with different clients and in different locations, Audit could be a great fit for you.
As an Audit Junior, you’ll experience the power of collaboration as you work with diverse teams on real projects, building lasting connections with colleagues and start off by learning the fundamentals, including:
* Working on audit and accounts preparation assignments with your team,
* Working closely with your mentor on audit planning memorandum,
* Analytical reviews,
* Drafting client letters,
* Preparing accounts and producing sets of financial statements.
* Studying towards Professional Qualification (ACA Level 7)
**Rewards That Resonate**
You’re more than a number to us; you’re someone with unique skills and aspirations. Our benefits are designed to support your wellbeing, foster your professional growth, and recognise the contribution you make.
* Agile working: Our flexible working policy gives you greater choice over how you structure your day. With core hours of 10am–2pm, you can start earlier or finish later to suit your needs, alongside the option to work from home up to two days a week. For trainees, we ask for full office attendance during the first six months to ensure you receive the training, support and experience needed for a strong start, with greater flexibility available after that.
* 30 days’ holiday, including bank holidays, plus the opportunity to buy or sell up to 5 days (28 days on a training contract, with the opportunity to buy 5 days).
* Full study support package: including exams, tuition, study leave days and materials.
* Employee recognition awards: Performance Award bonus and other recognition initiatives.
* Employee Assistance Programme: A free, confidential 24‐hour support service, including unlimited counselling sessions and access to virtual doctors for you and your family.
* And lots more!
**Are You Ready to Elevate Your Career?**
Apply now and be part of a team that celebrates diversity, champions innovation, and prioritises your success.
At MHA, we know that diversity, inclusion, and belonging lead to better decisions, stronger performance, and a workplace where everyone can feel included and thrive. That’s why we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.
**Disability Confident**
We are a Disability Confident employer. If you have a disability and meet the essential criteria for the role, we will progress you to the next stage of the process
If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process to help you perform at your best, please let us know and we will be happy to help.

## Description
**Build the commercial engine behind the next generation of autonomous chemical sensing.**
Mode Labs is developing an autonomous opto-chemical sensing platform for remote environmental monitoring. We are looking for a commercially astute, technically credible relationship-builder to lead our transition from field trials and early customer interest to repeatable commercial adoption.
### THE ROLE
You will own commercial strategy and business development as Mode Labs moves from product development into paid beta trials and first sales. Initially, you will work hands-on across customer development, propositions, pricing, marketing, CRM and forecasting, while building a disciplined route from technical trial to commercial purchase.
Reporting to the CEO and working as part of the senior leadership team, you will work closely with the CTO and product-development team to ensure that customer requirements shape our product roadmap and commercial priorities. The role begins as a senior individual-contributor and functional-lead position. As sales scale, you will build and lead the wider commercial team.
### WHAT YOU’LL DO
**Commercial Strategy, Sales and Revenue**
* Own the commercial strategy for the initial UK water and environmental-monitoring market, defining priority customers, propositions, routes to market and milestones.
* Build and convert the pipeline from early engagement through paid beta trials to commercial purchase.
* Lead customer discovery, proposals, pricing and negotiations, defining clear trial objectives and purchase criteria.
* Refine the business and revenue model, including pricing, recurring revenues, margins and customer lifetime value, and own pipeline and revenue forecasting.
**Customer Requirements, Product and Market Development**
* Establish a structured customer-requirements process, capturing use cases, performance needs, deployment constraints and procurement requirements.
* Work with the CTO and development team to translate customer and market evidence into a prioritised product roadmap, including analytes, product improvements and adjacent applications.
* Balance individual customer requests against wider market demand, technical effort and commercial potential.
* Track customers, competitors, regulation and market developments to identify new sectors, geographies and routes to market.
* Develop the longer-term commercial roadmap beyond the initial UK water market, identifying attractive adjacent sectors, geographies and partnership routes.
**Marketing, Evidence and Partnerships**
* Develop the marketing strategy and core sales collateral, turning beta trials into credible evidence, case studies and customer-facing content.
* Build trusted relationships across the water sector and relevant technical communities, representing Mode Labs with customers, partners and industry stakeholders.
* Identify and develop commercially valuable partnerships, pilots and grant-funded opportunities, working with the CEO and CTO where appropriate.
**Commercial Operations, Customer Success and Scale-up**
* Establish and own the CRM, sales process, qualification criteria, commercial metrics and reporting.
* Define and manage the customer journey from initial engagement through trial, purchase, deployment and repeat business.
* Work across engineering, manufacturing and quality to establish a scalable customer-support and service model covering commissioning, servicing, calibration and technical support.
* Define the structure, incentives and recruitment plan for the wider sales team as demand grows.
### WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
**Within your first 100 days, you will have:**
* Built a strong understanding of our technology, target markets, customers and commercial pipeline.
* Reviewed and prioritised the existing pipeline, with clear qualification criteria and CRM stages.
* Secured, or materially advanced toward contract, at least one paid beta trial with a priority customer.

## Job Description
About the Team
Newmark's Planning and Development team is one of the UK's largest fully integrated planning and development advisory teams, with over 120 professionals including more than 70 planning consultants and 45 surveyors. The team advises leading UK and international owners, developers, investors, and occupiers on planning transactions, development appraisal, and strategic advice across offices, residential, mixed-use, retail, and cultural schemes throughout London and the UK. You'll be joining a team working on some of London's most high-profile schemes, giving you broad exposure to major planning applications, strategic regeneration projects, and a real chance to develop into a chartered town planner.
Programme Overview
Newmark’s graduate planning programme is the perfect way to kickstart your career in town planning and development consultancy. You’ll gain hands-on experience across live planning projects, work with senior chartered town planners, and develop the skills and competencies needed to achieve your Chartered Town Planner (MRTPI) status through the Royal Town Planning Institute's accredited routes. Why Join Newmark?
• Structured, mentored path to qualification - You'll work towards Chartered Town Planner (MRTPI) status with dedicated mentors, exposure across project types, and hands-on learning experiences designed to build technical capability from day one. • Real responsibility, not just training - The programme is built around projects that challenge and inspire, with the autonomy to take initiative and the accountability to own your work - paired with regular 1:1 check-ins so you're never navigating it alone. • Global platform, local grounding - Based in our London West End office, you'll be part of one of the UK's largest integrated Planning and Development teams, with on-the-ground knowledge of Central London's planning environment. • High-profile project exposure - Newmark's Planning and Development team advises on major London schemes, including strategic regeneration and master planning projects, so joining now means exposure to prestigious, high-impact work from an early stage.
## Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities
• Conducting site visits and appraisals, and supporting pre-application and due diligence advice on development sites • Assisting with the preparation and submission of planning applications, representations, and supporting planning statements • Researching and analysing national, regional, and local planning policy to support advice on development proposals • Drafting sections of planning statements, appraisals, and client reports for senior review • Liaising with clients, local planning authorities, architects, and other professionals as part of multidisciplinary project teams • Maintaining accurate records and project data to support the wider Planning and Development team's pipeline • Working towards RTPI chartership requirements - logging structured training and experience, and meeting regularly with a designated mentor • Gradually taking on more client-facing responsibility as competency and confidence build across projects
Who We’re looking for
• Ambition and drive to excel, with a clear commitment to working towards Chartered Town Planner (MRTPI) status • Strong analytical and research skills, comfortable working with planning policy, data, and development appraisals • Excellent written and verbal communication • Commercial curiosity - an interest in London's planning environment and development landscape, and how policy and politics shape decision-making • Initiative and accountability - the confidence to take ownership of tasks while knowing when to ask for guidance Application Process
• Submit an online application including CV and answer a few short screening questions • MS Teams interview with one interviewer • In Person Interview with two assessors
Compensation & Benefits
We offer a supportive and rewarding environment ensuring that our graduates have the tools, guidance, and benefits needed to grow both personally and professionally.
• Competitive salary aligned with industry standards • Performance related staff profit share scheme • Wellbeing allowance which can be used for either physical or mental wellbeing activities • 26 days’ holiday, plus Bank Holidays and days at Christmas and New Year. • 1 paid volunteering day per year to help give back to our local communities • Pension scheme membership (after initial probationary period) • Access to Peppy for you and your partner • Life and Accident insurance • Group income protection scheme • Private Medical Insurance • Critical Illness Cover • Wellbeing Allowance • Interest Free Season Ticket Loan • Interest Free Rental Deposit Loan • Employee assistance programme • Enhanced maternity and paternity pay after probation period • Professional subscription (MRICS) paid for by the firm

The Firm’s core hours are from 10.00 a.m. to 4.00 p.m. and you may choose to start and end your day around these hours, provided you still do your 7.25 hours per day (e.g. 8.00 am – 4.30pm, 10.00 am – 6.30 pm). This position also involves out of hours working on an ‘as necessary’ basis.

Greater London, United Kingdom
## Job Description
As HR Systems Analyst, you will support the continued development of Oracle HCM and connected HR systems. You will work closely with HR Operations, Payroll, HR Business Partners, and IT to improve the quality, usability and effectiveness of our people systems. This role offers genuine breadth. One day you may be helping to resolve a system configuration issue; the next, you could be supporting to improve onboarding journeys across multiple countries, producing HR reporting, or developing clear operating procedures for our HR Shared Services team.
## Responsibilities
**What you will do**
* Provide functional support for Oracle HCM and related HR technology, investigating user queries, system issues and process failures.
* Support HR system changes from initial requirements through testing, implementation, user communications and post-implementation review.
* Partner with technical teams to help configure and improve HR processes, including employee and manager self-service, workflows, absence and leave processes, benefits and approvals.
* Review HR system data for accuracy, completeness and consistency; identify root causes of issues and help implement sustainable controls and improvements.
* Create and maintain recurring and ad hoc HR reports, data extracts and dashboards for HR, Payroll, Finance, leadership and regulatory reporting.
* Support data gathering and validation for key workforce reporting, including diversity-related analysis, while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data governance.
* Work with Payroll and HR Shared Services to understand the downstream impact of system changes and ensure effective data reconciliation and hand-offs.
* Help design, document and improve employee lifecycle processes, including onboarding, benefits enrolment, leave and family-related processes, organisational changes and employee records.
* Develop practical process documentation, standard operating procedures, user guidance and knowledge materials that enable consistent, high-quality HR service delivery.
* Support employee and manager communications relating to HR systems, benefits and new processes, ensuring information is accurate, clear and easy to use.
* Coordinate with external providers and internal technical teams to track incidents, enhancements, access issues, system configuration and service improvements.
* Work across legal entities and countries, identifying where HR processes need local variation while maintaining appropriate global consistency.
* Bring a continuous-improvement mindset: challenge manual workarounds, identify recurring themes and recommend practical, scalable solutions.
## Qualifications
**What you will bring**
**Essential experience and skills**
* Experience in an HR systems, HRIS, HR data, people operations or HR shared-services role.
* Experience using and supporting an enterprise HR system; Oracle HCM experience is preferred.
* Strong understanding of core HR processes, including employee lifecycle administration, onboarding, benefits, absence or leave and organisational data.
* Experience investigating system or data issues and working with technical teams, providers or internal stakeholders to resolve them.
* Strong Excel and data-analysis skills, including reviewing large datasets, reconciling information and identifying exceptions or trends.
* Experience producing HR reports, management information, data extracts or dashboards.
* Experience supporting process mapping, process documentation, SOP development or employee/manager guidance.
* Strong written communication skills, with the ability to turn technical or policy information into clear, practical content.
* Excellent attention to detail, sound judgement and a strong commitment to confidential handling of employee information.
* A collaborative style and confidence working with a broad range of stakeholders, including HR, Payroll, Finance, IT, senior leaders and external suppliers.
**Desirable**
* Oracle HCM experience across Core HR, Benefits, Absence, Journeys, Helpdesk, reporting, security or workflow.
* Experience supporting system configuration, release management, user acceptance testing or regression testing.
* Knowledge of HR and payroll interfaces, data reconciliation and system controls.
* Experience with Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps, SharePoint, Jira or case-management technology.
* Knowledge of GDPR, HR data governance, data quality controls and audit requirements.
* Experience supporting a multi-entity, multi-country or matrix organisation.
* Experience designing onboarding journeys, benefits communications or employee-facing HR content.

* Solid commercial experience with React and TypeScript, with a preference for explicit types that stay closely aligned with the database schema rather than relying on .

* Comfortable working with a server-first approach. We use server components wherever possible, with client components only where they are genuinely needed, and data fetching structured around appropriate suspense boundaries.
* Experience working within established UI patterns and shared components. We use our own components for tables, modals, inputs and other interface elements, and use design tokens rather than hardcoded values.
* A strong approach to accessibility. Accessibility is a requirement, not a follow-up task, particularly because many of our users work on mobile devices, under pressure and sometimes with poor connectivity.
* Good judgement about engineering risk. You should understand the difference between a low-risk change that can be shipped quickly and a change that requires additional review, testing or a more careful release plan.
* Clear written communication. We value documented functions, useful design notes and comments that explain why a decision was made rather than simply repeating what the code does.

* Experience with Next.js App Router and React server components.
* Deeper Postgres experience, including indexes, query plans, performance and safe migrations on larger tables.
* Experience introducing or improving automated testing and CI practices.
* Experience building multi-tenant, role-based or feature-gated permission systems.
* Experience in education, health, social care or another regulated or sensitive domain.
* Experience working directly with AWS services.

* Apply data minimisation when designing features and deciding what information needs to be stored, processed or displayed.
* Treat access controls and permissions as a core engineering responsibility.
* Avoid unnecessary exposure of sensitive information in logs, test data, tooling or internal workflows.
* Handle production data carefully and follow agreed processes when investigating issues.
* Preserve auditability where actions or changes affect safeguarding, attendance, case records, finance or compliance.
* Raise concerns where an implementation could introduce unnecessary privacy, safeguarding or security risk.

# Senior Technical Architect (Privacy)
London, United Kingdom | Customer Experience
### ### Strength in Trust
OneTrust’s mission is to enable innovation through the responsible use of data and AI. We believe that ensuring data is trusted shouldn’t slow teams down—it should accelerate what’s possible. This led us to develop the first technology platform for responsible data use in 2016. Today, with AI representing the latest and most impactful expansion of data yet, OneTrust is once again redefining what responsible innovation looks like. OneTrust, the AI‐Ready Governance PlatformTM, unifies regulatory intelligence, automation, and connected governance workflows so businesses can continue to move at the speed of AI while ensuring good governance to prevent data misuse at scale. Trusted by thousands of organizations worldwide, OneTrust is shaping the future where trusted data becomes a transformative force for business and society.
### **The Challenge**
We are looking for a Senior Technical Architect (Privacy) to join our Technical Advisory team (part of Customer Success). This is a customer-facing role for someone who combines a strong technical foundation with attention to details, and the ability to build trust with customers.You will work with privacy, legal, compliance, and technology stakeholders to understand business objectives and challenges, assess maturity and platform adoption, and provide clear recommendations across privacy processes, operating models, workflows, data, and integrations. You will act as a trusted advisor and product expert without owning hands-on implementation or configuration.Previous privacy or OneTrust expertise is valuable, but it is not the defining requirement for this role. We are looking for someone with the attitude, consultancy skills, and technical capability to learn the privacy domain quickly and become a trusted advisor.**### Your Mission**
* Lead outcome-focused discovery, advisory engagements, workshops, and expert sessions with customers.
* Clarify customer objectives, constraints, stakeholders, and desired outcomes before recommending a path forward.
* Translate business and regulatory needs into practical recommendations for privacy processes, workflows, data, integrations, and OneTrust capabilities.
* Explain solution options, dependencies, trade-offs, and implications for scale at the appropriate level of detail.
* Assess customer readiness, adoption barriers, process maturity, and solution direction; recommend pragmatic next steps.
* Create clear, decision-ready deliverables such as current-state assessments, future-state recommendations, reference architectures, process guidance, and reusable patterns.
* Build trusted relationships and communicate confidently with both technical and executive audiences.
* Partner closely with Customer Success, Product, Sales, Support, Professional Services, and other specialist teams to deliver consistent customer outcomes.
* Capture recurring customer needs and translate them into feedback, enablement content, playbooks, and product opportunities.
* Maintain clear advisory boundaries: provide strategic framing, product expertise, and guidance while enabling customers or delivery partners to execute implementation.
**### You Are** **#### Your Experience Includes
:**
* 5+ years of experience in consulting, technical advisory, solution consulting, customer success, business analysis, transformation, or another customer-facing problem-solving role.
* A strong technical background in enterprise software (ideally SaaS), systems, data, workflow design, integrations, APIs, solution architecture, or a related field.
* A consultative approach: you listen carefully, ask effective questions, structure ambiguity, and turn complex problems into clear recommendations.
* Strong learning agility and a constructive attitude, including curiosity, ownership, humility, resilience, and openness to feedback.
* The ability to connect customer objectives to practical technology and operating-model decisions.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt the message for executive, functional, and technical audiences.
* Independent but also a team player
* Experience influencing stakeholders and collaborating across functions without direct authority.
* BA/BS in a related subject is required
**Extra Impressive:**
* Experience in privacy, data protection, privacy operations, privacy technology, or a closely related field.
* Experience with OneTrust Privacy Automation or comparable privacy-management platforms.
* Familiarity with privacy regulations and frameworks
* OneTrust certifications or relevant privacy credentials such as CIPP/E, CIPM, CIPT
* Experience advising enterprise customers on adoption, optimization, governance, or value realization.
* Experience creating reusable advisory playbooks, reference architectures, or enablement materials.
* Experience in using software for reporting and task management, such as Salesforce
### Where we Work
We are embracing an office-first culture, encouraging three days a week in office for most roles, with meaningful opportunities to collaborate and celebrate in person.Each role may have specific requirements or flexibility depending on the scope of the position, so we encourage you to verify this with your recruiter during your first interview.

As an employee at OneTrust, you will be part of the OneTeam. That means you’ll receive support physically, mentally, and emotionally so that you can do your best work both in and out of the office. This includes comprehensive healthcare coverage, flexible PTO, equity RSUs, annual performance bonus opportunities, retirement account support, 14+ weeks of paid parental leave, career development opportunities, company-paid privacy certification exam fees, and much more. Specific benefits differ by country. For more information, talk to your recruiter or visit onetrust.com/careers.
### Resources
Check out the following to learn more about OneTrust and its people:
* OneTrust Careers on YouTube
* @LifeatOneTrust on Instagram
### Your Data
You have the right to have your personal data updated or removed. You also have the right to have a copy of the information OneTrust holds about you. Further details about these rights are available on the website in our Privacy Overview**.**You can change your mind at any time and have your personal data removed from our database. In order to do this you must contact us and let us know you wish to be removed. The request should be made on the Data Subject Request Form. Recruitment fraud warning: OneTrust is aware of scams involving false offers of employment with our company. The fraudulent jobs, interviews and job offers use fake websites, email addresses, group chat and text messages. Be aware that we never ask candidates for personal information, IDs or bank information during the interview process. We do not interview prospective candidates via instant message or group chat, and do not require candidates to purchase products or services, or process payments on our behalf as a condition of any employment offer. Please note that any legitimate interview availability requests will come directly from a OneTrust recruiter with an "@onetrust.com" email address. You may also receive legitimate emails from "@us.greenhouse-mail.io". Recruiters will only reach out to candidates who have applied for a role through our ATS (Greenhouse) or prospects via LinkedIn InMail. Job offers will come from a recruiter and may have a "@docusign.net" email address. For more information or if you have been targeted please reach out to askrecruiting@onetrust.com.

When you join OneTrust you are stepping onto a launching pad — the countdown has begun. The destination? A career without boundaries working alongside a diverse and inclusive crew who is passionate about doing meaningful work. As a pioneer, your voice and expertise will help chart the direction of an entirely new category. Our commitment to putting people first starts with you. Your growth is part of the mission. Our goal is to give you the power to embark on the next phase of your uniquely, unique career.
